Preface to the *Brief Liturgical Hymn for the Five-Part Recitation of the Buddha’s Name in the Pure Land* Composed at the Jingtu Yuan of Changjing Monastery: Now, the Tathāgata’s establishment of the teachings, whether extensive or concise, accords with the capacities of sentient beings and ultimately returns to the true mark (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*).
As for those who have attained true non-arising,
who could possibly rival them? Nevertheless,
the *nien-fo* samādhi is the truly unsurpassed, profound, and wondrous gate of dhyāna.
Using the name of Amitābha, the Dharma King, and his forty-eight vows as the Buddha-work,
he delivers sentient beings through the power of his vows.
Therefore, the sounds of the five assemblies flow through the eternal palace,
and the pure teachings universally moisten the sands of worlds.
Thus, the Avataṃsaka Sūtra says:
From the three stages of worthiness up to the unsurpassed bodhi of all Buddhas,
none arise apart from mindfulness of the Buddha, mindfulness of the Dharma, and mindfulness of the Sangha; therefore,
in such sutras as the Lotus Sutra and the Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra, it is said:
There are those who perform the Buddha-work through sounds and speech;
furthermore, since sound, name, phrase, and sentence constitute the essence of all teachings,
how could they be the same as the "purple-golden countenance" sought by scholars of today?
To categorize everything as possessing form is like pointing at the crest-jewel with one's finger; it is to mistake the teaching for mere words.
To speak of "formlessness" while abandoning true form is likewise a delusion.
To argue that there is no sound is to grow weary of the Brahma-sound;
to claim birth is unconditioned is to say that practice has lost its way.
To fall headlong into the mountain of heterodoxy would indeed be most lamentable.
Now, however, it is not so.
Furthermore, the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā* says:
The six perfections, the myriad practices, and all wholesome dharmas are none other than causes for Buddhahood.
This is the sincere and true mantra of Śākyamuni and all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
it is sufficient to serve as a basis for faith and reverence.
This may be practiced accordingly;
now, following the *Sūtra of Immeasurable Life*,
we shall practice the five-assemblies recitation of the Buddha’s name.
If one performs the ritual extensively,
it is fully detailed in the three-fascicle *Ritual Manual for the Five Assemblies*.
This includes the "Preface to the Extensive Explanation of the Invocation and Praise of Amitābha and the Contemplation Sūtra."
The questions, answers, and clarifications of doubts are all contained within that text;
it must be transcribed in full for study and circulation to future generations.
If one performs the ritual procedures in an abbreviated manner...
Relying on this very text,
all persons who perform ritual acts—
whether monastics or laypeople— should act accordingly.
The group should consist of no more than six or seven people, and no fewer than three or five.
Select those with good voices who understand the liturgy.
All must maintain dignified and orderly deportment, sitting upright with palms joined, focusing their minds single-mindedly on the visualization of the Buddha.
Chant with a unified voice and in perfect harmony;
do not laugh or look around;
give rise to a mind of genuine compassion and salvation.
Do not act out of desire for fame or profit.
Let the assembly designate one person as the presiding master (zhuāngzhǔ) to lead the ritual services for the *Zhuāngyán jīng* and the *Fǎzàn*.
One must know the proper sequence:
one person serves as the assistant seat;
he oversees the incense and lamps, strikes the chime, and leads the chanting of praises in unison.
The person in charge of supervision must first burn incense, ring the chime, and invoke the assembly of holy beings. Then,
the presiding person should recite the Buddha’s name once and address the assembly, saying:
I respectfully address the assembly at this place of practice:
you must all arouse a heart of utmost sincerity, sit upright with palms joined,
and visualize Amitābha Buddha and all the worthy sages as if they were standing before your very eyes.
If one can apply the mind in this manner, then the worthy sages will descend,
and the dragons and devas will protect and keep one in mind,
as one listens to and hears the recitation of the sutras and the performance of Dharma rites.
May all beings, upon hearing these words,
immediately extinguish immeasurable sins and attain immeasurable merit;
may their minds open and their understanding be clarified, so that they swiftly realize the profound Samādhi of Buddha-remembrance.
Having attained the patience of non-arising (anutpattika-dharmakṣānti) and acquired the great dhāraṇī,
he was fully endowed with the six pāramitās and sovereign supernormal powers.
Having finished speaking, he immediately struck the chime.
Having finished the *Brahma-saṃstuti*,
recite the names of Amitābha Buddha, Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta,
and Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva thirty or fifty times each.
Thereafter, with a sincere heart, perform prostrations and make a request.
Next, having completed the adornments, recite the Buddha's name as before;
one must then observe the number of disciples in that dharma-assembly.
Whether by day or by night, whether extensive or concise,
there is a ritual for inviting the presiding master of the *maṇḍala* for the sake of some virtuous undertaking.
One must know this for certain:
at different times, perform the adornments extensively and engage in recitation.
When sitting at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), there may be two sessions, three sessions, or even many sessions.
Regarding the *Amitāyurdhyāna-sūtra*:
For each sitting and each invocation,
the scattering of flowers, the music, and all the hymns of praise must be recited from memory;
this cycle shall be repeated again and again.
The sutra recitations must be thoroughly mastered; one must not consult the text at the last moment.
Only the *Wuhui Miaoyin* (Five-Assembly Sublime Sound) may be performed alone in a single sitting, provided it is done without vocalizing the words.
This applies if following the rule of a single sitting.
When performing the ritual for opening the sutras and the Dharma, one should observe whether it is to be done extensively or concisely;
then, all [the participants] should recite in sequence,
beginning with the scattering of flowers and the playing of music.
The scattering of flowers and music, each seated once;
the various jewel-birds with their marks and signs of excellence;
the five assemblies of Vimalakīrti.
The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* and *Svalpaprajñāpāramitā*, as well as the praises from the *Pratyutpanna-buddha-saṃmukhāvasthita-samādhi-sūtra* and the *Nirvāṇa-sūtra*,
are recited; for each two lines, one strikes the chime while remaining seated.
Praise of the Joy of the Pure Land and the Six Sense Faculties;
Praise of the Joy of the Western Paradise;
Praise of the Joy of Leaving Home, etc.
The four-line verses serve as the standard;
the music for the ritual arena consists of only a single line.
This applies to all hymns following the *Contemplation Sutra* on Amitābha.
All must harmonize by recollecting the Buddha during the third assembly.
When the various hymns have been chanted and one wishes to disperse,
one should immediately chant the *Dōjō-raku* (Joy of the Ritual Site).
The sound should be loud;
one must recite the name of Amitābha Buddha three hundred times or more during the third session.
Finally, chant the "Text for Dedication and Aspiration" by the Tiantai Master Zhizhe, which praises the West.
To dispel these [distractions]:
the wise must cultivate a deep revulsion for birth and death,
and practice the samādhi of mindfulness of the Buddha through correct recollection.
For the sake of all beings within the Dharma-realm— the enemies and kin of the six realms of existence—
I vow that they may be reborn together in Sukhāvatī and swiftly attain unexcelled Bodhi.
With single-minded devotion, I shall study and master the true sounds of the Five Assemblies.
It shall be transmitted to the future to extensively deliver all classes of beings.
If one does not study under a teacher but grants it indiscriminately to others,
one will mislead later students and cause them to lose the essential tenets.
This will instead invite blame and fail to benefit the field of merit.
I universally exhort all monastics and laypeople, both present and future,
to extensively perform the five assemblies of true sound.
The Samādhi of Buddha-Recollection cultivates both principle and phenomena.
Recollecting both with marks and without marks is precisely to be in accord with the Middle Way and the correct contemplation of the true mark (bhūtalakṣaṇa).
Question: What benefit is there in recollecting the Buddha during the five assemblies?
Furthermore, what does this symbolize?
The answer is:
It is precisely within this very life that one is able to become free from the afflictions of the five turbidities.
Eliminating the five sufferings and severing the five hindrances;
cutting off the five destinies and purifying the five eyes;
perfecting the five faculties and accomplishing the five powers.
One attains the five liberations that constitute the requisites for Bodhi and can swiftly accomplish the fivefold Dharma-body;
such is the power of the five assemblies of mindfulness of the Buddha.
Supreme and peerless,
throughout this single lifetime,
he shall suddenly cast off his final body as an ordinary person.
Upon being born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, one enters the noble stage of a bodhisattva,
attains non-retrogression, and swiftly reaches enlightenment.
Truly, the Buddha’s entrustment of this matter shall never be in vain.
How does one attain long life? And by what causes and conditions Does one obtain a vajra-like indestructible body And great, firm, and stable power?
How does one, regarding this sutra, Ultimately reach the other shore?

The ultimate principle and true Dharma are of one suchness;
yet, as the vows to transform beings and benefit people differ,
I, Śākyamuni, appeared in response within this turbid world.
Amitābha appears in the Pure Land; thus,
while the pure and the defiled are distinct,
the benefit bestowed is uniform.
If there were a teaching that was easy to practice and easy to realize,
it would truly be the Pure Land school;
yet even that Western realm is sublime and beyond compare.
As for that land, it is adorned with the hundred treasures and utilizes the nine grades of lotus blossoms to gather in sentient beings.
As for its name and title:
It can sweep away a thousand calamities; its sound opens the five assemblies to gather in all beings.
Therefore, those who invoke its name shall be constantly protected by the Buddhas of the ten directions.
For those who vow to be born in that land,
extraordinary flowers and five-colored clouds vie to support their seats;
thus we know.
The compassionate vow of Amitābha is inconceivable;
it truly may be said that it opens the transverse gate to the three realms.
Having cut off the direct path of the four modes of birth,
the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges extend their tongues to bear witness,
exhorting one to mind Amitābha and be born in the Buddha-land.
If this pure teaching were not proclaimed by the Buddhas wherever they may be,
how could those who have not yet heard it be made to hear it, and those who have not yet seen it be made to see it?
The intent of the present practice of *nienfo* (recollection of the Buddha) lies precisely here.
I pray that Śakra, Brahmā, and the World-Protectors will guard the nation and its people;
that the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas, will regulate the winds and rains.
May it be so that the Emperor’s wheel-treasure shall fly hither.
Spearheads are sheathed and armor laid aside;
the benevolence of Shun’s reign drenches the myriad nations from afar,
and the influence of Yao’s era extends throughout the eight wildernesses.
The Prince’s voice resounded like successive peals of thunder;
the wills of the various kings were as firm as massive boulders;
and the silver pavilions of the Princesses shone with brilliant luster.
May you, O Minister, forever stabilize the pivot of state affairs so that there may be no military conflict;
may your integrity shine ever more brightly.
May you eternally assist under the sky of Yao as a high official and court attendant.
Clouds fly across the provincial halls; stars reflect upon Mount Tiantai.
The high-ranking generals possess distinguished merit;
their glory renews itself daily.
The platform exceeds a hundred paces in height, surpassing that of high officials;
the horses are divided by color like camels, and their robes contain embroidered patterns.
May you quickly accept these modest consolations as we assist in governance and share in the concerns of state.
His pure reputation resounds afar.
Master Chan’s water of meditative concentration is limpid and pure;
he dwells within the river of Chan, and his compassionate breeze cannot be contained.
The sun of wisdom hangs long;
the mountain of Dharma Master’s Way grows ever steeper,
and the ocean of his wisdom becomes ever deeper.
Dwelling among humans and devas,
he constantly serves as a boat and oar;
his preceptor’s Vinaya and the pearl of his precepts are ever pure.
The principle of the illuminated vehicle is free from shame;
the pond of meditative concentration is eternally pure—
how could it fail to surpass the green waters of the Canglang River?
The three pillars of the monastery illuminate the Sanskrit script;
they have long cultivated harmony with the assembly of disciples who follow the Mahāyāna.
Receiving their pure influence,
the monastic community lived in harmony like water and milk;
the various ācāryas brought the three studies to perfect clarity.
May the lamp of wisdom shine forever;
may you propagate this teaching so that we may together proceed to the Pure Land.
May the moon of the nuns' precepts remain ever bright.
Concentrating the spirit, one enters meditative absorption;
the Way-tree flourishes eternally,
and the flower of enlightenment forever displays its beauty.
May the merit of you gentlemen be as vast as a mountain,
and your longevity equal that of the cypress and the crane.
May the ladies and mistresses possess jade-like constitutions that flourish through all seasons.
Unchanging for a thousand autumns,
the pure-faith men and women have repeatedly heard the Buddha’s name through karma as vast as the sands of the Ganges.
Like ice melting away,
immeasurable fields of merit increase in accordance with one's mindfulness of the Buddha.
The samādhi of the accomplishment of observing karma manifests before him.
Whether sitting or walking, he constantly beholds all Buddhas;
yet he prays that the sun of the Buddha may remain high-suspended.
The Wheel of Dharma is widely proclaimed;
those in the dark realms find relief from suffering,
and the hearts of those on Mount Pīṭhaka are at peace.
May all those who have hopes see their wishes fulfilled;
may all that they contemplate be successfully realized in due time.
May all sentient beings and conscious beings together transcend the causes of outflows (*āsrava*).
May all in this realm and other directions together aspire to be born in peace and happiness.
Amitābha Buddha’s ocean of merit is boundless.
The great assembly, with sincere devotion,
all together recited the name of Amitābha Buddha.

In the fourth month of summer, in the first year of the Dali era,
[the author] began this work at the Pratyutpanna Samādhi Practice Hall on Mount Wutai’s Amitābha Terrace.
Based upon the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*, he composed these questions:
In which text does the "five assemblies" of nianfo appear?
The answer is:
the *Mahā-amitāyus-sūtra* states:
There were some jewel trees with mother-of-pearl for their roots and purple gold for their trunks.
The branches are made of white silver;
the twigs are made of lapis lazuli;
and the leaves are made of crystal.
Coral forms the flowers and agate forms the fruits;
they are arranged in rows, facing one another.
The stalks face one another;
the branches correspond to one another;
the leaves lean toward one another.
The flowers bloom in harmonious succession;
the fruits ripen in perfect correspondence.
Their radiant splendor and brilliant colors are such that they cannot be fully beheld.
A pure breeze frequently issued forth the sounds of the five musical scales;
their subtle *gong* and *shang* tones naturally harmonized with one another,
all causing one to mindfully recollect the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha.
Those who hear this sound shall attain the profound *dharmakṣānti* (patience regarding the Dharma),
abide in non-retrogression, and proceed until they reach the path of Buddhahood.
Furthermore, I shall explain the fivefold recitation of the Buddha's name (*pañca-samāja buddhānusmṛti*).
Fifth, "assembly" (samāja) refers to a gathering.
Those five kinds of sounds constitute the assembly.
From slow to fast, one should think only of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha,
without any other distracting thoughts.
To contemplate is non-contemplation;
this is the Buddha’s gate of non-duality.
Sound is impermanent.
This is the primary meaning. Therefore,
throughout the day one recites the Buddha's name,
always remaining in accord with true nature.
Throughout the day one aspires for rebirth,
constantly applying oneself to the subtle principle;
such is the manner in which the resolve for awakening is generated.
The celestial māras will surely descend to beat the Dharma drum;
the earth will quake in six ways and a profusion of four kinds of flowers will rain down.
The attainment of perfect enlightenment upon the adamantine jewel throne is now to be expected.
Therefore, the *Contemplation Sūtra* says:
"If there are those who practice mindfulness of the Buddha,
they should know that..."
This person is a white lotus among humanity;
they are called rare and extraordinary.
[They are like] Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
As their supreme friends,
they shall sit at the site of enlightenment and be born into the family of all Buddhas;
for this reason, the Tathāgata constantly dwells within the ocean of samādhi.
Holding the net, he said to his father, the King:
"Your Majesty is now practicing dhyāna."
One should simply practice mindfulness of the Buddha;
how could this be the same as abandoning thought to seek non-thought,
or abandoning birth to seek non-birth?
To seek the Dharma-body apart from its marks and signs,
or to seek liberation apart from words and letters—
those who act thus abide in the view of nihilism.
By slandering the Buddha and destroying the sutras,
they have committed the karmic deeds that form a casket of suffering and shall fall into the Avīci Hell.
Those who cultivate the Way must be careful not to disparage it and must be reverent not to deceive.
Furthermore, the *Buddha-samādhi-sāgara Sūtra* states:
This Samādhi of Contemplating the Buddha is the protection for those who have broken the precepts;
it is the reliance for those who have lost the Way.
It is a great heroic general among the thieves of affliction;
it is the source from which the Śūraṅgama King and hundreds of thousands of samādhis arise,
and is also called the mother of all samādhis.
It is also called the King of All Samādhis;
it is also called the Concentration Authorized by All Buddhas;
it is also called Tathāgata-dhyāna.
It is clear that this is not the dhyāna of the two vehicles or the non-Buddhists;
this can be known through faith.
This is the sound of the nianfo (recitation of the Buddha's name) during the five assemblies.
When the momentum of the breath reaches its limit,
the elder [practitioner] simply maintains a relaxed mindfulness; when the momentum becomes small and gradually shortens, [the practitioner should likewise maintain relaxed mindfulness].
This refers to gradually increasing the intensity of the recitation;
one must understand this principle.
First, recite "Namo Amitābha Buddha" in a level tone and at a slow pace.
The second assembly: recite "Namo Amitābha Buddha" with a level, even tone and a relaxed pace.
The third assembly: recite "Namo Amitābha Buddha" at neither a slow nor a hurried pace.
In the fourth session, recite with gradually increasing urgency: *Namo Amitābha Buddha*.
In the fifth session, recite the four characters with even greater urgency: *Amitābha Buddha*.
Upon completing the five sessions of mindfulness of the Buddha, recite the various praises of the precious birds.
The Adornments of Ultimate Bliss, interspersed with jewels—Amitābha Buddha! Truly wondrous, hearing what has never been heard before—Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha!
Precious birds descend from the sky to praise the Buddha’s assembly—Amitābha Buddha! Their voices mournful, elegant, and clear, stirring the hearts of men—Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha!
Day and night they raise their voices without ceasing—Amitābha Buddha! Every word and every phrase share the same principle—Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha!
Some speak of Amitābha Buddha as the five faculties and the seven factors of enlightenment; Some speak of Amitābha Buddha as the eightfold noble path and the gate of compassion.

Amitābha Buddha! Some speak of Amitābha Buddha as being in other lands and free from the evil realms; Some speak of Amitābha Buddha as sealing the gates of hell and leading beings to heaven and humanity.
Amitābha Buddha! Some speak of Amitābha Buddha as the perfection of scattered virtues; Some speak of Amitābha Buddha as entering deep dhyāna through concentration and wisdom. Amitābha Buddha!
Some say Amitābha Buddha practiced asceticism for a long time; Some say Amitābha Buddha is the cause of unsurpassed *bodhi*.
When Amitābha Buddha’s Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas hear this Dharma, Amitābha Buddha manifests emanations everywhere to turn the wheel of Dharma.

Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha! May this turning of the wheel of Dharma continue uninterrupted. Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha! May the assembly at the site of enlightenment increase in longevity. Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha!
May the assembly turn their minds toward the Pure Land of Amitābha Buddha; Holding incense and flowers in hand, they go to the West, to Amitābha Buddha—Amitābha Buddha!
The Buddha-land is pure, manifesting from the mind, inconceivable; Its various adornments arise within the mind, inconceivable.
Vimalakīrti pressed the earth with his toe, and the trichiliocosm was inconceivable; He sat upon a flower pedestal within the ocean-like nature of space, inconceivable—Vimalakīrti!
The square chamber in the city of Vaiśālī is inconceivable; There dwells a layman named Vimalakīrti, who is inconceivable.
Vimalakīrti manifests a physical illness, which is inconceivable; The king, princes, and all the countless śrāvakas and bodhisattvas come to visit him, which is inconceivable.
No one is able to go and inquire after his illness, for Vimalakīrti is inconceivable.
Only Mañjuśrī entered into the inquiry and posed the inconceivable challenge: "What is the cause of the householder’s illness? It is inconceivable. Vimalakīrti replied:

"The illness arises from ignorance and craving; it is inconceivable. My illness is neither existent nor non-existent; it is inconceivable. Vimalakīrti spoke extensively on how the body is an impermanent phenomenon; it is inconceivable.
That the body is a composite of the aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and sense-bases (*āyatana*) is inconceivable—thus spoke Vimalakīrti.
It is inconceivable that a Bodhisattva’s hair-tip can contain a great ocean; It is inconceivable that Mount Sumeru can be contained within a mustard seed;
It is inconceivable that Vimalakīrti could cast a world beyond other directions with his hand; It is inconceivable that the goddesses in the room realized the non-arising of phenomena.

Vimalakīrti, in ages as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the past, was Amitābha Buddha; Through diligent practice of austerities, he cultivated the marks and signs of his body. Amitābha Buddha! Amitābha Buddha!
Now I have attained the realization of Amitābha Buddha of the Unseen Summit; Furthermore, I give rise to Amitābha Buddha of the Deep Blue Hair with Swirling Whorls;
Amitābha Buddha of the Ūrṇā-hair between the brows, the color of crystal; Amitābha Buddha of the Right-Spiraling Turquoise Tube;
Amitābha Buddha whose teeth are like white jade pendants, all even and closely set; Amitābha Buddha whose tongue-attribute extends long, covering the face; Amitābha Buddha.
The Buddha’s heart is a red lotus; seated upon golden ground is Amitābha Buddha. Pure and radiant, he divides the light of the sun; Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha.
In the first assembly, his voice is level and harmonious; Amitābha Buddha. In the second, he performs the most wondrous and pure chanting;
Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha. In the third, his movements are like the playing of music; Amitābha Buddha. In the fourth, he intones with focused effort; Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha.
Fifth: Raise your voice and recite the name of Amitābha Buddha with all haste. Upon hearing these five assemblies, one awakens to the realization of non-arising.
Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha—once you reach the Western Land, you shall receive bliss. Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha—never again will you transmigrate into the pit of suffering.

Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha—when resolving to practice mindfulness of the Buddha, the matter must be firm. Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha—at the moment of death, you will certainly ascend upon the golden boat. Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha.
I dedicate these merits so that all sentient beings may go to the land of Amitābha Buddha; Directly facing the West, they shall sit upon precious lotus flowers—Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha!
The Western World is truly sublime—Amitābha Buddha; The sentient beings of that land must not be looked down upon—Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha!
Holding flowers in their robes, they offer them to the Buddha—Amitābha Buddha; Returning to their own lands, they eat and practice walking meditation—Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha!
Arousing the mind to recite the Buddha’s name to deliver all sentient beings—Amitābha Buddha! May these five assemblies spread widely—Amitābha Buddha! Amitābha Buddha!
May those in the six realms and the three miserable paths all be gathered in—Amitābha Buddha! Within the Lotus Assembly, the True Name is enshrined—Amitābha Buddha! Amitābha Buddha!
The joy of the Pure Land, the joy of the Pure Land— The inconceivable Pure Land, the joy of the Pure Land!
Amitābha dwells in the jeweled towers of the Pure Land; may we incline our hearts, moment by moment, seeking the joy of the Pure Land.
Upon reaching that realm of the three insights and eight liberations, the joy of the Pure Land, one forever parts with the five turbidities—what further cause for sorrow?
Joy of the Pure Land! Joy of the Pure Land! Joy of the Pure Land! The Pure Land is inconceivable; joy of the Pure Land!
The joy of the Pure Land: jeweled towers, jeweled pavilions, and jeweled canopies held aloft; The joy of the Pure Land: pond waters with golden sands reflecting the bottom, pure and serene;
The joy of the Pure Land: the Dharma melody constantly offered at all times; Within the assembly of lotus flowers, one preaches non-arising—this is the joy of the Pure Land.
Joy of the Pure Land! Joy of the Pure Land! The inconceivable Pure Land—joy of the Pure Land!
The joy of the pure land of jeweled terraces, jeweled pavilions, and pure pearls; The joy of the pure land of a majestic, precious body with a golden form;
The joy of the pure land where Bodhisattvas are born by transformation and play the jade lute; The joy of the pure land where gentle breezes perform the fivefold melody of True Suchness.
Joy of the pure land! Joy of the pure land! The inconceivable pure land—joy of the pure land!

The flowing waters and rippling waves encircle the precious terraces—joy of the Pure Land! The precious halls radiate light and the jade doors stand open—joy of the Pure Land! After this, recite quickly:
"The Compassionate Lord hears from afar the children of the three realms—joy of the Pure Land! All must resolve to be reborn there—joy of the Pure Land! Joy of the Pure Land! Joy of the Pure Land!
The Western Pure Land is most blissful—joy of the Pure Land! Joy of the Pure Land!
The body of Amitābha is vast and boundless—joy of the Pure Land! His face resembles refined gold and the *utpala* flower—joy of the Pure Land!
His eyes are like blue lotuses and the four great oceans—joy of the Pure Land! His halo and emanated Buddhas exceed the sands of the Ganges—joy of the Pure Land!
Joy of the Pure Land, joy of the Pure Land! The Western Pure Land is most blissful—joy of the Pure Land!
The Great Compassion of Amitābha’s Original Vow is the bliss of the Pure Land; Ordinary beings here do not perceive this bliss of the Pure Land— Bliss of the Pure Land!
Bliss of the Pure Land! Bliss of the Pure Land! Fearing that sentient beings might emerge into the world too late, The bliss of the Pure Land:
under the spring trees of Amitābha, the flowers of awakening bloom; The bliss of the Pure Land: sitting upon jeweled terraces within the pond of merit.

Seeking liberation before the courtyard of samādhi, the joy of the Pure Land; In the mani palace, prostrating to the Tathāgata, the joy of the Pure Land— The joy of the Pure Land, the joy of the Pure Land!
In the western Pure Land there is exceeding happiness, the joy of the Pure Land;
In the west, wondrous birds are beyond counting, the joy of the Pure Land— White cranes, peacocks, and kalaviṅkas, the joy of the Pure Land.
Parrots and kalaviṅkas proclaim the wondrous Dharma; the joy of the Pure Land. From their voices emerge the syllables of the Mahāyāna; the joy of the Pure Land.
The joy of the Pure Land, the joy of the Pure Land, the joy of the Pure Land! In the Western Pure Land there is supreme happiness;
the joy of the Pure Land. The Honored Name of the Tathāgata is most distinct; the joy of the Pure Land. It flows everywhere throughout the worlds of the ten directions; the joy of the Pure Land.
Whoever merely utters the name shall all attain the joy of the Pure Land. Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta come in person to welcome them to the joy of the Pure Land;
the joy of the Pure Land, the joy of the Pure Land! The Western Pure Land is exceedingly joyful; the joy of the Pure Land!
The assembly of Amitābha possesses universal compassion; the joy of the Pure Land! Their pity for sentient beings is most profound; the joy of the Pure Land!
