All sentient beings are delivered and liberated; the joy of the Pure Land! By chanting the name, sins are immediately eliminated;
the joy of the Pure Land! The joy of the Pure Land, the joy of the Pure Land! In the Western Pure Land there is supreme happiness; the joy of the Pure Land!
Amitābha sits upright within a precious golden pavilion; the joy of the Pure Land! Bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges roam on all sides; the joy of the Pure Land!
The nine classes of beings receive the light and hear the sublime Dharma; the joy of the Pure Land! Those who hear it awaken to understanding and are forever free from sorrow;
the joy of the Pure Land! The joy of the Pure Land! The joy of the Pure Land! The Western Pure Land is exceedingly blissful;

the joy of the Pure Land! In the Western Pure Land there is no clamor or dust; the joy of the Pure Land! When sentient beings arrive, they immediately sever greed and hatred; the joy of the Pure Land!
The Pure Land is always joyful with assemblies of virtuous beings and bodhisattvas; there are no evil realms, nor enemies or kin—this is the joy of the Pure Land.
Joyful is the Pure Land! Joyful is the Pure Land! In the Western Pure Land there is supreme happiness. Joyful is the Pure Land!
Flower-banners hang from eight sides, adorned with golden bells; joyful is the Pure Land! Above and below they resonate in harmony, producing wondrous sounds—joyful is the Pure Land!
All who hear it say it is called the joy of the Pure Land’s bliss. Throughout long kalpas, the names of all sufferings are not heard;
the bliss of the Pure Land! The bliss of the Pure Land! The bliss of the Pure Land! The Western Pure Land is exceedingly joyful; the bliss of the Pure Land!
If ordinary beings can reach the Western Pure Land, the bliss of the Pure Land, Then the sins of kalpas as vast as dust motes will be extinguished; the bliss of the Pure Land!
Possessing the six supernormal powers, one attains the bliss of mastery in the Pure Land; Forever eliminating old age and illness, one leaves behind impermanence in the bliss of the Pure Land.
Bliss of the Pure Land! Bliss of the Pure Land! The Western Pure Land is most joyful; bliss of the Pure Land!
In the Western Pure Land, one is free from the womb; bliss of the Pure Land! As soon as sentient beings arrive, they emerge from the lotus pedestal; bliss of the Pure Land!
The joy of the Pure Land: ascending the jeweled throne by seeking light in the highest grade; The joy of the Pure Land: the flowers finally bloom when rebirth below has exhausted all obstacles.
Joy of the Pure Land! Joy of the Pure Land! In the Western Pure Land there is supreme happiness. Joy of the Pure Land!
In the Western Pure Land there are sevenfold railings. Joy of the Pure Land! Adorned with the seven treasures in hundreds of varieties. Joy of the Pure Land!
The land is made of lapis lazuli with golden boundaries; the joy of this pure land! The various towers and pavilions connect to the open heavens; the joy of this pure land! The joy of this pure land!
The joy of this pure land! The western pure land is exceedingly joyful;

the joy of this pure land! The western pure land is rare throughout the ten directions; the joy of this pure land! Exert yourselves with single-minded focus and harbor no doubts; the joy of this pure land!

Those of superior capacity realize the patience of the non-arising of dharmas; the joy of the Pure Land! Those of lower capacity exhaust their obstacles upon rebirth and enter the unconditioned Pure Land;
the joy of the Pure Land! The joy of the Pure Land! The Western Pure Land is most blissful; the joy of the Pure Land!

In the Western Pure Land there is nothing that surpasses it; the joy of the Pure Land! While Jambudvīpa is filled with those who suffer extreme misery and commit many sins, there is the joy of the Pure Land!
If you wish to be born in the joy of the Pure Land beyond the three realms, You need only focus your mind on the joy of Amitābha’s Pure Land.
Joy of the Pure Land! Joy of the Pure Land! The Western Pure Land is most blissful; Joy of the Pure Land! I am pure and joyful! I am pure and joyful!
Beholding the emptiness of the mind, one realizes the world: I am pure and joyful!
Contemplating that the eye-faculty is eternally pure, I am pure, blissful, and joyful; The realm of forms has no coming and is originally empty, I am pure, blissful, and joyful;
The nature of form is originally without obstruction, I am pure, blissful, and joyful; Neither coming nor going is the True Teaching, I am pure, blissful, and joyful.
Contemplating that the ear-faculty is eternally pure, I am pure, blissful, and joyful; The realm of sounds has no coming and is originally empty, I am pure, blissful, and joyful.
The nature of sound is originally unimpeded; I am pure and joyful. Neither coming nor going is the True Teaching; I am pure and joyful.
I clearly perceive that the faculty of the nose is eternally pure; I am pure and joyful. The realm of fragrance has no coming and is fundamentally empty;
I am pure and joyful. The nature of fragrance is originally unimpeded; I am pure and joyful. Neither coming nor going is the True Teaching; I am pure and joyful.
Contemplating that the tongue-faculty is ever pure, I am pure, blissful, and joyful; The realm of taste has no coming and is fundamentally empty—*I am pure, blissful, and joyful*.
The nature of taste is originally without obstruction—*I am pure, blissful, and joyful*; Without coming and without going is the True Teaching—*I am pure, blissful, and joyful*.
Contemplating that the body-faculty is ever pure, *I am pure, blissful, and joyful*; The realm of touch has no coming and is fundamentally empty—*I am pure, blissful, and joyful*.
The nature of touch is originally unobstructed; my purity and bliss— Without coming or going is the True Dharma;
my purity and bliss. Observing the faculty of mind, it is ever pure; my purity and bliss— The Dharma-realm has no origin and is fundamentally empty;
my purity and bliss. The nature of phenomena is originally unobstructed; my purity and bliss— Without coming or going is the True Dharma; my purity and bliss. Recite this rapidly thereafter.
Forgetfulness causes the eye-faculty to turn toward forms with effort; forgetfulness causes the ear-element to be dragged by sounds, making it difficult to know.

Forgetfulness causes the nose to scent odors and the tongue to be stained by flavors with effort; forgetfulness causes consciousness to perceive body-touch and the mental objects to shift, making them difficult to know—difficult to know, yet one must exert effort!
I universally exhort you to mindfully recite Amitābha’s name and cultivate merit.
Forgetfulness and delusion surge like waves, constantly drowning us; strive! The fierce flames of affliction burn perpetually, difficult to discern;
for this reason, strive within the prison of the three realms of saṃsāra! Born into the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death, we are constantly tormented;
difficult to discern, difficult to discern—strive! I universally exhort you to mind Amitābha and cultivate merit.
Having the good fortune to encounter a virtuous friend who diligently points toward the gate of Western bliss so difficult to recognize—strive!
If you wish to swiftly transcend the suffering of birth and death, strive with single-minded devotion to recite the Buddha’s name and sever greed and anger;
it is difficult to recognize, truly difficult to recognize—strive! I universally exhort you to recite the name of Amitābha and cultivate merit.
The true gate to Amitābha’s precious land is now open; strive! Within the pond of the seven treasures stands a terrace of the seven treasures;
it is difficult to discern its thousand petals and myriad colors; strive! Half are still within the light, half emerge from the water;
it is difficult to discern, difficult to discern—strive! I universally exhort you to recite the name of Amitābha and cultivate merit.
Amida’s five assemblies strive to save the Sahā world; All who hear this can cause the sprout of the Way to grow.
It is difficult to recognize; may the multitude incline their hearts and strive to recite the Buddha’s name with diligence!
It is difficult to recognize; it is difficult to recognize; strive on! I universally exhort you to recite Amida’s name and cultivate merit.
Jambudvīpa is turbid and evil, unfit for lingering; strive! Everywhere one hears only the sounds of manifold sufferings;
it is difficult to recognize [the truth], so strive instead to single-mindedly recite the name of Amitābha! In this life you shall go directly to the City of the Precious Lotus;
it is difficult to recognize, difficult to recognize—strive! I universally exhort you to recite the name of Amitābha and cultivate merit.
In the western jeweled palace, by the jeweled pond pavilion, strive! The birds of the jeweled grove understand human sentiment;
it is difficult to recognize the parrots’ harmonious chanting as they praise the Three Bodies. Strive! From within their voices, the Mahāyāna sūtras are produced;
it is difficult to recognize, difficult to recognize—strive! Universally exhort all to recite the name of Amitābha and cultivate merit.
In the Western Quarter, the precious trees with their precious roots and trunks are most wondrous; The precious flowers and precious nets are so distinct they are difficult to discern;
The rows of precious leaves interlace one another, most wondrous; Precious fruits emerge in successive layers, born through transformation, difficult to discern—most wondrous!
I universally exhort you to cultivate merit for Amitābha.
Exert yourselves at the jeweled pond with its jeweled banks and jeweled lotuses; Exert yourselves at the jeweled stairs and jeweled floor where the golden sand is difficult to perceive.
Though there may be obstacles from previous lives that hinder the descent [to rebirth], exert yourselves!
It is difficult to perceive, difficult to perceive—exert yourselves! Universally exhort one another to mind Amitābha and cultivate merit.
In the Western Pure Land, rain-like robes fall; strive! Within the jeweled palaces, they fly after one’s body in the void; it is difficult to discern.
In a single thought-moment, a hundred flavors arrive according to the mind; strive! For what reason do sentient beings who depart there remain so few?
It is difficult to discern—difficult to discern! I universally exhort you: recite the name of Amitābha and cultivate merit.

The joy of the True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma— The inconceivable joy of the True Dharma of Śākyamuni Tathāgata while on the path of practice; The inconceivable joy of the True Dharma of his ascetic practices throughout kalpas;
The joy of the True Dharma of suddenly relinquishing body and wealth to seek the wondrous Dharma— Only a Buddha and a Buddha can truly know this joy of the True Dharma.
The joy of the True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma; The inconceivable joy of the True Dharma.
The youth of the Snowy Mountains, Śākyamuni, For the sake of seeking half a verse, sacrificed his golden body—this is the joy of the True Dharma.
Good friends seeking the Dharma together through both causes—this is the joy of the True Dharma. It was truly because he saved the poor man in his own land—this is the joy of the True Dharma.
The joy of the True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma— The inconceivable joy of the True Dharma!
Through the power of compassion, the five yakṣas gave their bodies as an offering; this is the joy of the True Dharma. King Dānaśūra abandoned his kingdom and renounced his glory;

this is the joy of the True Dharma. Sucandra cut his own body to save his parents; this is the joy of the True Dharma. He gave away his wife and children, crying out "Dhana"; this is the joy of the True Dharma.
The joy of the True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma! The inconceivable joy of the True Dharma!
Candraprabha made a vow to sacrifice his thousand heads for the joy of the True Dharma; Śākyamuni did not harbor grief even when his bones were ground to powder for the joy of the True Dharma;
Furthermore, as Śibi, he gave his own life in place of a dove for the joy of the True Dharma; He will not rest until he has realized Bodhi for the joy of the True Dharma!
The joy of the True Dharma! The joy of the True Dharma! The inconceivable joy of the True Dharma!
King Ratnarāja cut his own body to light a thousand lamps—what joy of the True Dharma! Sāṃkṛtyāyana threw himself from a cliff to feed the beasts of prey—what joy of the True Dharma!
With a compassionate heart, he opened himself to give away his five viscera—what joy of the True Dharma! I ask you, O sentient beings: can you not know this joy of the True Dharma?
The joy of the True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world;
the Teacher’s ascetic practices were truly difficult to discuss. The joy of the True Dharma—reflecting deeply, one cannot bear to question it.

The joy of the True Dharma—what was previously described by you, that calculation of affairs, is the joy of the True Dharma. Every single thing is the cause of Śākyamuni; this is the joy of the True Dharma.
The joy of the True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma enables one to transcend the world;

through generosity, ethical discipline, and long-term cultivation, there is the joy of the True Dharma. Through patience, diligence, and never departing from meditative concentration, there is the joy of the True Dharma.

Through ascetic practices and arduous cultivation until merit is fulfilled, there is the joy of the True Dharma. In discussing the duration of kalpas, we do not speak of years; this is the joy of the True Dharma.
The Joy of the True Dharma, the Joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world; it is the joy of the True Dharma.
When Śākyamuni Tathāgata was on the path of practice, it was the joy of the True Dharma. Through many eons of asceticism, he alone surpassed all others;

it was the joy of the True Dharma. In every instance, he cultivated unsurpassed deeds; it was the joy of the True Dharma. He realized Bodhi and transcended the world; it is the joy of the True Dharma.
The joy of the True Dharma! The joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world; the joy of the True Dharma!
The Original Teacher practiced asceticism and attained the Tathāgata; the joy of the True Dharma! Transmitted from reality to reality without artifice or falsehood;
the joy of the True Dharma! Realizing the unsurpassed fruit of Bodhi; the joy of the True Dharma! Dividing one’s body into ten billion forms to save Jambudvīpa; the joy of the True Dharma!
The joy of the True Dharma! The joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma enables one to transcend the world;
the joy of the True Dharma descends from heaven to the royal palace. The joy of the True Dharma! Entrusting his being within the womb during Queen Māyā’s dream, The joy of the True Dharma!
In the rear garden, he clings to the Aśoka tree; The joy of the True Dharma! From her right side, he is immediately born with a truly sublime countenance. The joy of the True Dharma!
The joy of the True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world;
the joy of the True Dharma is the first seat upon birth for a Wheel-Turning King. The joy of the True Dharma shakes heaven and earth and radiates light;
The joy of the True Dharma manifests as the emanation body of Śākyamuni. The joy of the True Dharma causes all disciples everywhere to leave behind impermanence. The joy of the True Dharma!
The joy of the True Dharma! The joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world; the joy of the True Dharma!
Nine dragons spout water to wash the divine embryo; the joy of the True Dharma! Heavenly beings and humans honor him, supporting the infant in their armpits;

the joy of the True Dharma! Immediately he walks seven paces to the east and west; the joy of the True Dharma! With every lift and placement of his feet, he treads upon lotus pedestals; the joy of the True Dharma!
Having grown up, I left the city and entered the Snowy Mountains to delight in the True Dharma; I practiced austerities for another full six years to delight in the True Dharma.
Clad in grass garments and eating hemp and wheat, I delighted in the True Dharma; Sitting cross-legged with mindfulness gathered, I returned to meditative absorption to delight in the True Dharma.
Delight in the True Dharma! Delight in the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world—delight in the True Dharma!
The inconceivable joy of the True Dharma, which makes one’s emaciated form flourish; The joy of the True Dharma, when the cowherd maiden offered herself with milk-rice;

The joy of the True Dharma, having finished eating, he bathed himself in the river; The joy of the True Dharma, as Śakra pressed down the branch of the tree from the sky— Joy of the True Dharma, Joy of the True Dharma, Joy of the True Dharma!
The True Dharma can transcend the world; it is the joy of the True Dharma.
The joy of the True Dharma, which attains Buddhahood through this cause and radiates light; The joy of the True Dharma, spoken from the Golden Mouth to transform sentient beings;

The joy of the True Dharma, extensively expounding the subtle and wondrous teachings of the Three Vehicles; The joy of the True Dharma, circulating throughout the Sahā world. The joy of the True Dharma, for the True Dharma can transcend the world.
The joy of the True Dharma! The joy of the True Dharma! The joy of the True Dharma! The joy of the True Dharma, which can transcend the world. The joy of the True Dharma!
The joy of the True Dharma for over ninety years after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa; In that land, they walk and roam through the five regions, the joy of the True Dharma.

I universally exhort all sentient beings to diligently practice mindfulness of the Buddha, the joy of the True Dharma; I also teach them to uphold the precepts and cultivate dhyāna, the joy of the True Dharma.
The joy of the True Dharma! The joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world; it is the joy of the True Dharma.

Ordinary beings see the Buddha as gradually fading away, yet they delight in the True Dharma; The Tathāgata observes them and returns once more to manifest the delight of the True Dharma through the display of impermanence and the return to the Reward Land.

Obeisance to the Delight of the True Dharma! Obeisance to the Delight of the True Dharma! Obeisance to the Delight of the True Dharma! The True Dharma is able to transcend the world; obeisance to the Delight of the True Dharma! Obeisance to the Delight of the True Dharma!
Obeisance to the Delight of the True Dharma! Obeisance to the Delight of the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world; obeisance to the Delight of the True Dharma!
The joy of the True Dharma for one thousand years after the Parinirvāṇa; The joy of the True Dharma as the teachings spread to this land;
The joy of the True Dharma as sentient beings recite, rely upon, and practice it; The joy of the True Dharma that reveals the fruit of enlightenment and birth in heaven— The joy of the True Dharma!
The joy of the True Dharma! The joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world—the joy of the True Dharma!

Therefore, know that to escape the cage of afflictions and attain the joy of the True Dharma— Practicing each according to the fundamental teachings of the Original Teacher is the joy of the True Dharma;
If one follows the general path without cultivation, one becomes a Buddha; this is the joy of the True Dharma. Examine for yourself whether the principle is penetrated or not;

this is the joy of the True Dharma. The True Dharma can transcend the world; this is the joy of the True Dharma. The joy of the True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma is able to transcend the world; this is the joy of the True Dharma.
The joy of the True Dharma: first, as one goes forth, it severs the affliction of craving; The joy of the True Dharma: it destroys the mountain of ignorance and the self-view.
The joy of the True Dharma: here in Jambudvīpa, it is free from attachment; The joy of the True Dharma: having attained it for the first time, one frequently transcends the world.
The joy of the True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world; the joy of the True Dharma!
The nature of untainted wisdom is the eternally true joy of the sublime Dharma; long dwelling in ignorance, it has been hidden by defilements—the joy of the sublime Dharma.

Sentient beings commit boundless transgressions—the joy of the sublime Dharma. If one seeks to become a Buddha while erring, one forever looks toward the joy of the sublime Dharma—the joy of the sublime Dharma, the joy of the sublime Dharma!
The sublime Dharma can transcend the world—the joy of the sublime Dharma.
Ordinary beings, with their inverted views, do not contemplate the joy of the True Dharma;
Whatever they do, they do not know the joy of the True Dharma for themselves, and thus their evil karma remains entirely undiminished. The joy of the True Dharma! The joy of the True Dharma!
The joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world; the joy of the True Dharma!
The Mahāyāna teaching of non-conceptual emptiness is the joy of the True Dharma; Emptifying ignorance and craving is the joy of the True Dharma.
Sentient beings with inverted views confuse pure gold with dross—this is the joy of the True Dharma; Denying cause and effect to deceive the common masses—this is the joy of the True Dharma.
Joy of the True Dharma! Joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world—joy of the True Dharma!
Do not resent the plainness of these words, yet harbor anger; the True Dharma is joy. Investigate and examine them thoroughly; all of this is truly the joy of the True Dharma.
Having seen those who act erroneously, I point them toward the True Dharma as joy. In the end, they shall surely enter the heart and core of the True Dharma as joy.
The True Dharma can transcend the world; the True Dharma is joy. The True Dharma is joy, the True Dharma is joy. The True Dharma can transcend the world; the True Dharma is joy.

Just as one who suffers from a great illness seeks the joy of the True Dharma for its removal; One who receives the fire-moxa treatment to uproot the very seeds of affliction finds the joy of the True Dharma.

Having been able to awaken through hearing the Dharma, one finds the joy of the True Dharma; Through meditative concentration, one is born in the Pure Land where nothing remains—this is the joy of the True Dharma.
The joy of the True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world—the joy of the True Dharma.

Sentient beings, strive to recollect Amitābha; the joy of the True Dharma is supreme. There is nothing more urgent or swift than the joy of the True Dharma, which opens the nine grades for the Western Land.
The joy of the True Dharma allows one to leave Saṃsāra with all sins and hindrances intact.
Joy of the True Dharma! Joy of the True Dharma! Joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world; the joy of the True Dharma!
Sentient beings follow the Buddha to the West, where there is the joy of the True Dharma; Because of even a speck of dust of past karma, it naturally perishes—there is the joy of the True Dharma.
The Tathāgata’s power of vows personally bestows grace—there is the joy of the True Dharma. Hearing the Dharma, one awakens to the Way and realizes the eternal—there is the joy of the True Dharma.
Joy of the True Dharma! Joy of the True Dharma! Joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world—there is the joy of the True Dharma.
Universally proclaiming to all the sons of the Buddha in the *maṇḍala*: the joy of the True Dharma! Each and every one should resolve to attain Bodhicitta:
the joy of the True Dharma! The true essence of the True Dharma must be emulated and studied: the joy of the True Dharma! Clearly seeing that those of external paths are incapable [of it]:

the joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world: the joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma is able to surmount the mundane world: the joy of the True Dharma!

What is it that is called the True Dharma? The joy of the True Dharma. If this principle is the true teaching, then the joy of the True Dharma is good; one must now discern between right and wrong regarding the joy of the True Dharma.
Examine each point with meticulous care; do not remain in confusion regarding the joy of the True Dharma. The True Dharma can transcend the world; it is the joy of the True Dharma.
The joy of the True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma. The True Dharma is able to transcend the world; it is the joy of the True Dharma.
Observing the precepts and practicing seated meditation is called the True Dharma; the joy of the True Dharma. Mindfulness of the Buddha and attaining Buddhahood is the True Vehicle;

the joy of the True Dharma. Not grasping at the words of the Buddha is called an outsider’s path; the joy of the True Dharma. Denying cause and effect while viewing things as empty is [the view of] the True Dharma;

the joy of the True Dharma. The True Dharma can transcend the world; the joy of the True Dharma. The joy of the True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma, the joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma is able to transcend the world; the joy of the True Dharma.
How is it that Chan and Vinaya are the True Dharma? The joy of the True Dharma. The Samādhi of Buddha-remembrance is the True Vehicle; the joy of the True Dharma.
To see one's nature and realize the mind is to be a Buddha; the joy of the True Dharma. How can such principles be inconsistent with the joy of the True Dharma?
The joy of the True Dharma! The joy of the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world; the joy of the True Dharma.

With every sound of reciting the Buddha’s name, one plants the seeds of the Buddha and enjoys the True Dharma; Sitting in meditation and upholding the precepts require true effort to enjoy the True Dharma.

If you do not cultivate it, you will fail to become a Buddha; enjoy the True Dharma! It is like a hungry person vainly shielding themselves from the wind; enjoy the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world;
enjoy the True Dharma! Enjoy the True Dharma! Enjoy the True Dharma! Enjoy the True Dharma! The True Dharma can transcend the world; enjoy the True Dharma!
The bliss of the West, the bliss of the West! The pure land of the West is inconceivable. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
Śākyamuni universally exhorts us to mind Amitābha: the bliss of the West. The intent is for all beings to emerge from the river of craving. The bliss of the West:

upon the superior lotus pedestals, one beholds the Compassionate Lord and the sons of the Buddhas. All who arrive have done so because they recited the Buddha’s name extensively. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
The West is joyful, the West is joyful! The Pure Land of the West is inconceivable. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world.
In the West, progress on the Path surpasses that of Sahā. The West is joyful! There, one is free from the five desires and malevolent demons.

The West is joyful! To attain Buddhahood, one need not toil at various good deeds. The West is joyful! Sitting upright upon the lotus throne, one contemplates Amitābha. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world.
The bliss of the West, the bliss of the West! The pure land of the West is inconceivable; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world, do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!

In the five turbidities, practice leads to much regression; the bliss of the West— Is not equal to reciting the Buddha’s name and going to the West. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world, do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!

Upon arriving there, one spontaneously attains perfect enlightenment; the bliss of the West— Returning to the sea of suffering, one acts as a bridge and raft. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world, do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
The bliss of the West, the bliss of the West! The pure land of the West is inconceivable; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world, do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
The world of Jambudvīpa cannot endure long; the bliss of the West— The causes and conditions of evil karma fill it daily.

O sons of the Buddhas, though you may perform such virtues, Unaware, hell will already have formed before you. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world, do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
Joyful in the West, joyful in the West! The Pure Land of the West is inconceivable. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world;
do not cling to the pleasures of the human world! The joy of the Western Ultimate Bliss resounds! Throughout long eons, the names of all sufferings shall not be heard.

In the music and song of the drums of the Western Land, the space is filled with the sons of the Buddhas, Naturally harmonizing as they proclaim the Unsurpassed. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
The bliss of the West, the bliss of the West! The pure land of the West is inconceivable; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world, do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
Jambudvīpa is foul and evil, unfit for lingering; the bliss of the West— With its evil karma, anger, strife, and ignorance—the bliss of the West!

If you can single-mindedly recollect that Buddha, O sons of the Buddhas, In the precious realm of Amitābha, you shall realize non-arising; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world, do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
Delight in the West, delight in the West! The Pure Land of the West is inconceivable; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world, do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
In the West, the Land of Ultimate Bliss, are ponds of seven treasures; The water of eight virtues is inconceivable—delight in the West!

At the bottom lies a shore of golden sand, with fragrant trees and sons of the Buddhas; Lotus flowers emerge, giving birth to transformed beings—do not cling to the pleasures of the human world, do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
The West is blissful, the West is blissful! The Pure Land of the West is inconceivable; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world, do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
The Amitābha Pure Realm is most subtle and wondrous; the West is blissful! In the Golden World, the ground is made of lapis lazuli; the West is blissful!

Fragrant breezes blow through the rows of jeweled trees; the sons of the Buddhas, With the five musical modes, perform rare wonders; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world, do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
The bliss of the West, the bliss of the West! The Pure Land of the West is inconceivable. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!

In the Land of Ultimate Bliss, there are ponds of the seven treasures. The bliss of the West! When the flowers bloom, the lotuses are purple and their radiance shines forth. The bliss of the West! By focusing the mind on Amitābha, one ascends the precious throne.

O children of the Buddha, in an instant, one realizes the unconditioned without even being aware of it. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
The bliss of the West, the bliss of the West! The pure land of the West is inconceivable. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
Before the jade-green pavilion stands a terrace of the seven treasures—the bliss of the West! The youths of the various heavens vie with one another to come; the bliss of the West!

Each one holds flowers to make offerings to the Buddha, all these sons of the Buddhas. Everywhere they speak only of "Excellent!"—do not cling to the pleasures of the human world; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
The bliss of the West, the bliss of the West! The Pure Land of the West is inconceivable. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
Do not be surprised that we repeatedly exhort one another toward the bliss of the West.

Seeing people everywhere subject to impermanence, O sons of the Buddha, If you attain the profound samādhi of buddha-remembrance, you need not fear the three miserable realms, for there is the King of Equality. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
The bliss of the West, the bliss of the West! The Pure Land of the West is inconceivable; do not cling to the pleasures of the human realm, do not cling to the pleasures of the human realm!
Among all practices, this is the most urgent and essential: the bliss of the West. Nothing surpasses the Gate of the Pure Land in swiftness: the bliss of the West.

Not only did our Original Teacher speak it with his own golden mouth, but all the Buddhas of the ten directions have likewise transmitted and testified to it: do not cling to the pleasures of the human realm, do not cling to the pleasures of the human realm!
The bliss of the West, the bliss of the West! The pure land of the West is inconceivable; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world, do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!

With jeweled ponds and jeweled shores, most vast and level—this is the bliss of the West! The jeweled ground is made of lapis lazuli, shining with a thousand-fold brilliance—this is the bliss of the West!

I universally exhort all sentient beings to diligently recite the Buddha’s name, O children of the Buddhas! Amitābha will surely come to welcome you yourself; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world, do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
The bliss of the West, the bliss of the West! The pure land of the West is inconceivable; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world, do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
In this realm, if one person recites the Buddha’s name, the bliss of the West Will immediately have a lotus flower arise.

O sons of the Buddhas, Provided that one never regresses for even a single lifetime, this flower will return here to welcome you. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world, do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
The bliss of the West, the bliss of the West! The pure land of the West is inconceivable. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
One must urgently practice the recollection of the Buddha; do not be idle. The bliss of the West— If you wish to transcend the sea of suffering, you need a boat.

The bliss of the West— By chanting the name, one will certainly be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss, O sons of the Buddhas! Forever sever the flow of birth and death in Jambudvīpa. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
Return and go! There is joy in the West; The five turbidities of Jambudvīpa are but dust and ashes. The joy of the West is incomparable;
in that land of Western bliss, O sons of the Buddhas, upon arriving there, the flower-thrones shall open at will. Do not cling to human pleasures; do not cling to human pleasures.
Return and go! There is joy in the West; In Amitābha’s pure land, the jeweled palaces are opened. There is joy in the West.
All you sons of the Buddha who can turn your hearts toward mindfulness of the Buddhas, At the end of life, you will surely sit upon the golden platform.

Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world. Return! Return to the joy of the Western Land! The sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death press hard upon us;

the joy of the West is found by day and night diligently and single-mindedly reciting the Buddha’s name, O sons of the Buddha. In the palace of mani-jewels, pay homage to the Tathāgata. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world; do not cling to the pleasures of the human world.
Return and go back to the bliss of the West; who could wish to undergo the cycle of rebirth in the evil realms?

If you can recite the name of Amitābha, O sons of the Buddha, you shall be born in Sukhāvatī and sit upon a lotus throne. Do not cling to the pleasures of the human world—do not cling to the pleasures of the human world!
The bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi is supreme; I vow to be born there. By single-mindedly reciting the Buddha’s name, one shall behold Amitābha and experience immeasurable bliss.
I universally exhort you to turn your minds and vow to be born in the Pure Land; by dedicating your merit through mindfulness of the Buddha, you will be reborn together in immeasurable bliss.
I vow to be born in the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi. With single-minded devotion, mindfulness of the Buddha reveals Amitābha and immeasurable bliss.
Having wandered through the ages since time immemorial, I vow to be born in immeasurable bliss as I follow conditions through the six realms of saṃsāra.
May I be reborn through the joy of the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi*; With single-minded mindfulness of the Buddha, may I see Amitābha and his immeasurable bliss.
Not having met a virtuous friend who encourages rebirth, Who can exhort me to return to that immeasurable bliss?
May I be reborn through the joy of the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi*; With single-minded mindfulness of the Buddha, may I see Amitābha and his immeasurable bliss.

Recalling the fleeting pleasures of the heavenly realms, I vow to be reborn there; When merit is exhausted and death approaches, the five signs of decay appear— Recalling the immeasurable bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi, I vow to be reborn there.
With single-minded mindfulness of the Buddha, one beholds Amitābha—immeasurable bliss;
Recalling the suffering of dwelling within the human womb, I vow to be reborn there; The four snakes and six thieves compete to hasten my end—immeasurable bliss.
The bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi; may I vow to be born there. With single-minded devotion recollecting the Buddha, one sees Amitābha; such is immeasurable bliss.
Remembering the suffering of the asuras, hungry ghosts, and the realms of affliction—famine, emptiness, strife, and contention beyond measure— One seeks the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi;
may I vow to be born there. With single-minded devotion recollecting the Buddha, one sees Amitābha; such is immeasurable bliss.

Recalling the experience of being born as an animal, devouring one another—may I vow to be reborn there; Recalling the immeasurable joy of casting off life amidst the glare of blades and yet again pulling the plow—may I vow to be reborn in the joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi;
Recalling the immeasurable joy of seeing Amitābha by single-mindedly reciting the Buddha’s name—may I vow to be reborn there;

Recalling the experience of suffering for a long time in hell—may I vow to be reborn there; Recalling the immeasurable joy of being blown away by the winds of karma, unable to turn back—may I vow to be reborn there.
The bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi—may I vow to be reborn there! With single-minded mindfulness of the Buddha, one beholds Amitābha; such is its immeasurable bliss.
Or entering the cauldrons of boiling water and the furnaces of burning coals, one vows to be reborn there! Where surging waves and fierce flames roar like thunder; such is its immeasurable bliss.
The bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi—may I vow to be reborn there! With single-minded mindfulness of the Buddha, one beholds Amitābha; such is its immeasurable bliss.
Some climb the mountain of knives and grasp the trees of swords, vowing to be reborn there—what immeasurable joy!
Their skin, flesh, and bones turn to ash; what immeasurable joy! The joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi! With single-minded devotion they recite the Buddha’s name and behold Amitābha;

what immeasurable joy! I ask you: by what cause do you undergo such suffering? Vow to be reborn there—what immeasurable joy! Craving fish and loving meat, their karma follows them; what immeasurable joy!
The bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi; may I vow to be born there. With single-minded devotion recollecting the Buddha, one sees Amitābha; what immeasurable bliss!
Like molten copper poured into the mouth or a plowshare dragged across it—may I vow to be born there. Drinking wine and speaking falsehoods bring about such calamities;
what immeasurable bliss! The bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi; may I vow to be born there. With single-minded devotion recollecting the Buddha, one sees Amitābha; what immeasurable bliss!
Or lying upon an iron bed and embracing a copper pillar, may they vow to be born there—immeasurable joy for those who have come through the perversity of sexual misconduct.
May they vow to be born in the immeasurable joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi. May they vow to be born in the immeasurable joy of seeing Amitābha by single-mindedly recollecting the Buddha.
Or falling into the great Avīci Hell, may they vow to be born there—immeasurable joy throughout kalpas and long years with eyes never opening.
The bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi; may I vow to be reborn there. With single-minded mindfulness of the Buddha, one sees Amitābha; what immeasurable bliss!
The fire from above and the fire from below intersect and pass through; may I vow to be reborn there. Swords, wheels, and iron pestles fly toward one of their own accord;
what immeasurable bliss! The bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi; may I vow to be reborn there. With single-minded mindfulness of the Buddha, one sees Amitābha; what immeasurable bliss!

May those whose hearts are bitten by copper dogs and whose blood is devoured, vow to be reborn there; May those whose eyes are pecked out by iron crows and whose gills are pierced, vow to be reborn there.

The immeasurable bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi, The immeasurable bliss of seeing Amitābha through single-minded mindfulness of the Buddha— May all the assembly at this day’s *bodhimaṇḍa* vow to be reborn there.
The immeasurable bliss of having passed through kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
The Joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: I vow to be reborn there; With single-minded mindfulness of the Buddha, one beholds Amitābha—what immeasurable joy!
Celebrating this human life so difficult to encounter, I vow to be reborn there; It is like the first blooming of the udumbara flower—what immeasurable joy!
The Joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: I vow to be reborn there; With single-minded mindfulness of the Buddha, one beholds Amitābha—what immeasurable joy!

Precisely at this time, when the teaching of the Pure Land is rarely heard, I vow to be born there; Precisely at this time, when the Dharma-door of Buddha-remembrance opens the infinite bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi, I vow to be born there;
With single-minded devotion to Buddha-remembrance, one beholds Amitābha and experiences infinite bliss;

precisely at this time, when Amitābha’s great vows call out to me, I vow to be born there; Precisely at this time, when the great assembly turns their hearts with faith toward it, I vow to experience infinite bliss.
The Joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: May I be Vowed to Rebirth. With single-minded devotion recollecting the Buddha, one sees Amitābha;

infinite joy is precisely what we encounter today. Relying on the Sūtra, I praise and vow for rebirth. Precisely at this moment, I adorn the flowered altar; infinite joy is precisely what we encounter.
The Joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: May I be Vowed to Rebirth. With single-minded devotion recollecting the Buddha, one sees Amitābha; infinite joy.

Precisely at this time, when the site of practice is free from demonic interference, I vow to be reborn there; Precisely at this time, when free from illness and affliction, one can come to experience immeasurable bliss—the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi—I vow to be reborn there;
With single-minded devotion recollecting the Buddha and beholding Amitābha, one attains immeasurable bliss;

precisely at this time, when the merit of seven days is perfected, I vow to be reborn there; By means of the essential forty-eight vows, may we be led together to immeasurable bliss—I vow to be reborn there.
The Joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: I vow to be born there; Single-mindedly recollecting the Buddha, one sees Amitābha—immeasurable joy!
I universally exhort my fellow practitioners at the site of enlightenment to vow to be born there; Strive with diligence to turn your hearts and return home—immeasurable joy!
The Joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: I vow to be born there; Single-mindedly recollecting the Buddha, one sees Amitābha—immeasurable joy!

I ask, where is my homeland? I vow to be reborn upon the seven-jeweled terraces within the pond of Sukhāvatī; I vow to be reborn in the joy of immeasurable bliss and the joy of the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi*.

With single-minded devotion, I recite the Buddha’s name and behold Amitābha; I vow to be reborn in that joy of immeasurable bliss. In the midst of his causal practices, that Buddha established a great vow;
I vow to be reborn there. Upon hearing my name and remembering me, he will welcome all; I vow to be reborn in that joy of immeasurable bliss.
May I be reborn through the joy of the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi*; With single-minded devotion recollecting the Buddha, may I behold Amitābha and his immeasurable bliss.
Without distinction between the poor and the wealthy, may I be reborn; Without distinction between those of inferior wisdom and those of superior talent, may I enjoy immeasurable bliss.
Through the joy of the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi*, may I be reborn; With single-minded devotion recollecting the Buddha, may I behold Amitābha and his immeasurable bliss.

Without distinction, those who lack the karma for a pure land yet vow to be reborn therein; Without distinction, even non-Buddhists and icchantikas who desire the immeasurable bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi;

With single-minded mindfulness of the Buddha, seeing Amitābha and desiring the immeasurable bliss thereof—without distinction, those who have practiced asceticism for a long time and vow to be reborn therein;
Without distinction, those who have only today first given rise to the mind [of awakening] and desire the immeasurable bliss [of rebirth].
The joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: I vow to be reborn there; With single-minded devotion recollecting the Buddha, one sees Amitābha—immeasurable is this joy.

It makes no distinction between the learned or those who uphold the pure precepts; It makes no distinction between those who have broken the precepts or whose offenses are deep-rooted—immeasurable is this joy.
The joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: I vow to be reborn there; With single-minded devotion recollecting the Buddha, one sees Amitābha—immeasurable is this joy.
Simply turn your minds toward the Buddha, recite his name, and vow to be born in the Pure Land—this can transform rubble into gold;
may you vow to be born in the immeasurable bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi. With single-minded devotion, recite the Buddha’s name and behold Amitābha;

this is immeasurable bliss. I address the great assembly gathered here now: may you all vow to be born there. Those who share this same aspiration, may you seek one another soon; this is immeasurable bliss.
The Joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: I vow to be born there; With single-minded mindfulness of the Buddha, one sees Amitābha and his immeasurable bliss.
I ask you, where do you go to seek him? I vow to be born there; It is said that within Amitābha’s Pure Land lies immeasurable bliss.
The Joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: I vow to be born there; With single-minded mindfulness of the Buddha, one sees Amitābha and his immeasurable bliss.
I ask: by what cause can one be born there? I vow to be reborn there. It is said that through the practice of *nien-fo*, success is spontaneously achieved;
I vow to be reborn there in the joy of the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi*. By single-mindedly reciting the Buddha’s name, one beholds Amitābha;

I vow to be reborn there in immeasurable bliss. I ask: this present life is burdened with many karmic obstacles; how could the Pure Land be willing to admit me? I vow to be reborn there in immeasurable bliss.
The Joy of the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi*: I vow to be reborn there; With single-minded mindfulness of the Buddha, one sees Amitābha—immeasurable joy!
The Way is proclaimed: by chanting his name, sins are extinguished; I vow to be reborn there. It is like a bright lamp entering the darkness—immeasurable joy!
The Joy of the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi*: I vow to be reborn there; With single-minded mindfulness of the Buddha, one sees Amitābha—immeasurable joy!
I ask: can ordinary beings attain rebirth? I vow to be born there. How can a single thought bring light into the darkness?
The immeasurable bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi—I vow to be born there. By single-mindedly reciting the Buddha’s name, one beholds Amitābha;
this immeasurable bliss is reported as the removal of doubt through frequent recitation—I vow to be born there. Amitābha will certainly come close to you himself; this is immeasurable bliss.
The Vow for Rebirth through the Joy of the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi*; Single-mindedly recollecting the Buddha to behold Amitābha; The Infinite Bliss of the Pure Land.
End of the *Praise for the Ritual Procedures of the Five Assemblies for Reciting the Buddha’s Name*.
The Supplement to the *Praise for the Ritual Procedures of the Five Assemblies for Reciting the Buddha’s Name*.
Composed by the Śramaṇa Fazhao of Mount Nanyue at the Pure Land Cloister of Changjing Monastery in the Capital.
*Praise for the Sons of the Bodhisattva*. Alas, living beings! Alas, living beings!

The Bodhisattva-sons sport in the Western Quarter; within the encircling flower-pavilions, they go forth with patience and enter their dwellings without harboring anger. Within the encircling flower-pavilions, they cultivate only the Pure Land; the Bodhisattva-sons realize the body of purple-gold. Within the encircling flower-pavilions—within the encircling flower-pavilions—they contemplate the minds of sentient beings, the minds of sentient beings.
Sunk in the mud-bottom of ignorance, when will the Bodhisattva-sons awaken?

Having attained realization, they wrap the hearts of sentient beings within a thousand-fold, golden, swirling flower-pedestal; they wrap the hearts of sentient beings within a thousand-fold, golden, swirling flower-pedestal.

The waves are surging and difficult to restrain; where among the Bodhisattva-sons of the four continents do they not seek you out? They wind and turn within the flower-pedestals; within those winding flower-pedestals, which finger points to the land of Amitābha? A resounding joy!
There is not a single person who has passed through the suffering at the bottom of hell.
Alas for the sentient beings! Those who flee are many.
What can be done? O Heaven! What can be done? O Heaven!
Sentient beings share no causal connection with the Buddha;

though transformed by a thousand words and a hundred phrases, they cannot be saved. O Son of the Bodhisattva, know for certain that the sinner will roll about within the floral pedestal of the Yellow Springs. As he rolls within the floral pedestal, Amitābha constructs a great ship for him.

Churning to the very edge of the sea of suffering, the prow of the boat grows dark as it nears its submersion; yet the noble sons of Bodhisattvas deliver those who recite the Buddha’s name, winding through the enclosures of the flower terraces, winding through the enclosures of the flower terraces—from east to west across the pond, upon the terraces of a hundred jewels.
The pavilions of radiant light open in ten thousand layers.

For a moment, one gazes from within the pavilion upon the Bodhisattva, the Son of the Buddha who is to succeed him; he then returns to the hall to pay homage to the Tathāgata. He moves gracefully around the flower pedestals—around the flower pedestals—enveloped by red lotuses and blue lotuses.
Born upon the thousand-petaled lotus pedestal, he is sustained by Amitābha Buddha; he is sustained by Amitābha Buddha.

Long ago, there was a worthy man in a śāla grove; constantly dwelling in the mountain forests, in that śāla grove, hundreds of birds together proclaimed the name of the śāla grove, looking at one another like brothers.
There was a traveler on the side of the path who lost his footing and fell into a flowing spring;
clutching a rootless tree, he called out the name of Avalokiteśvara.
Hearing these words, a young deer immediately leapt into the water.
I say to you: mount the back of the deer; I shall carry you across to the other shore.
Once you have reached the other shore, at every step you must kneel before the deer.
There is nothing with which to repay the deer’s kindness; serve as its slave.
The deer is but an insect among the grass; do not employ it as a servant.
When hungry, it eats the hundred plants; when thirsty, it drinks from the flowing springs.
If you wish to repay the deer’s kindness, do not say, "The deer is here."
There was a king who suffered from a chronic ailment caused by his consort;
every night he saw a nine-colored deer,
and if he did not obtain this nine-colored deer, [he would die].
The great life-force is difficult to sustain.
The king issued an edict to assemble his ministers:
"Who knows of the nine-colored deer? Is there anyone who knows the deer's whereabouts?"
He divided the kingdom and bestowed a thousand pieces of gold;
Upon hearing these words, Nao-er joined his palms before the king and said:
"Your servant knows that the nine-colored deer always stays by the flowing waters; I beg Your Majesty to lead forth many soldiers."
This deer was extremely agile; the king, leading a host of one million soldiers, surrounded the four mountain forests.
The king drew his bow, intending to shoot the deer.
Listen to the words spoken by the deer:
"The king was Kāśyapa;
the deer was the Tathāgata."
Though your body dwells alone like a deer,
you are merely a person with the great affliction of craving.
In the past, I saved your life.
Who would have expected that today I would harm the body of this deer?
I transmit these words to you, black-headed creatures: it shall be difficult for us to repay this kindness in life after life.
I universally exhort all sentient beings within this place of practice: [to cherish one another].
Strive together to give rise to the Bodhicitta. The joy of the *maṇḍala*:
every member of the great assembly joins their palms. The joy of the *maṇḍala*: shattering one’s own body, one repays the kindness of Śākyamuni.
The joy of the *maṇḍala*: being able to attain the skillful means of compassion. The joy of the *maṇḍala*: pointing the way to the gate of happiness in the Western Pure Land.
The joy of the practice hall as the assembly disperses and those about to part; Exert yourselves and encourage one another to sever greed and anger—this is the joy of the practice hall.

Greed and anger are the causes and conditions that obstruct the Pure Land—this is the joy of the practice hall. Failing to attain liberation, one sinks forever into the depths—this is the joy of the practice hall.

Practicing together with mutual intimacy and mutual exhortation—this is the joy of the practice hall. Taking our final lives as the limit until we stand before the Buddha—this is the joy of the practice hall.
May this wheel of Dharma turn in succession; the joy of the maṇḍala! May the assembly at the maṇḍala increase in long life;
the joy of the maṇḍala! May we all together receive this happiness; the joy of the maṇḍala! Seeing, hearing, and rejoicing are likewise so;
the joy of the maṇḍala! May the assembly turn their minds toward the Pure Land; the joy of the maṇḍala! Holding incense and flowers in hand, they go to the West; the joy of the maṇḍala!
Attaining birth in the Pure Land, one repays the immeasurable kindness of the teacher; when a person can recite the Buddha’s name, the Buddha in turn recites Amitābha’s name.
With single-minded concentration on Amitābha, the Buddha knows the person’s immeasurable joy.

All who turn their hearts toward the peace and bliss of Amitābha, they shall immediately behold the true golden body of merit and virtue—immeasurable joy. The adornments of the Pure Land and the assembly of all the sages—Amitābha, Amitābha!
Amida Buddha, Amida Buddha—amidst immeasurable joy, a pavilion always stands before the traveler; having seen it, the practitioner’s heart rejoices.

Amida Buddha, Amida Buddha—at the time of death, one follows the Buddha from his seat upon the golden lotus; amidst immeasurable joy, in a single thought-moment, one ascends the dais to reach the Buddha’s assembly.

Amida Buddha, Amida Buddha—one immediately realizes non-retrogression and enters the stage of the Three Sages; amidst immeasurable joy, every flower in each and every pond is completely filled. Amida Buddha, Amida Buddha.
Flower upon flower always leads those who pass away to immeasurable bliss; How could one not rejoice in a hundred thousand kalpas with the Golden Flower?
Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha! I do not desire even a moment in hell for the sake of immeasurable bliss; May each remain half-seated, riding upon the petals of the flowers.

Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha! I await my fellow practitioners here in Jambudvīpa; Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha! Please convey these words to the practitioners of Saha: Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha!
Be diligent in every thought-moment and do not sleep; through this causal condition, one is born in the Pure Land.
Amitābha Buddha! Amitābha Buddha! May I be reborn in the joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi. May the sufferings of the three realms and six paths cease;
may I be reborn to deliver beings from Saṃsāra through manifold emanations. May I be reborn to manifest the eight phases of Buddhahood and save all sentient beings—this is immeasurable bliss.

May I be reborn in the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi; may the sufferings of the three realms and six paths cease, and may I be reborn in immeasurable bliss that has long been submerged throughout kalpas.
In every place, I hear only the sounds of birth and death; may I be reborn in the immeasurable bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi;
may the sufferings of the three realms and six paths cease, and may I be reborn in immeasurable bliss.
I vow to be reborn in the True Reward Land of Śākyamuni; May my body be shattered in gratitude for the immeasurable kindness of Śākyamuni.
I vow to be reborn in the immeasurable bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi; May the sufferings and hardships of the three realms and six paths cease.
I vow to be reborn in the immeasurable bliss where the bone across the mouth prevents speech; All is due to the lack of wholesome causes in previous lives. Immeasurable bliss!
May those who delight in the Pratyutpanna Samādhi vow to be reborn there; may the sufferings and hardships of the three realms and six paths cease, and may immeasurable bliss be attained.
May those with the forms of animals—furred or horned—vow to be reborn there; may their bodies be subjected to various beatings by others, yet attain immeasurable bliss.
May those who delight in the Pratyutpanna Samādhi vow to be reborn there; may the sufferings and hardships of the three realms and six paths cease, and may immeasurable bliss be attained.

May all myriad practices turn back together so that I may attain the vow of rebirth; May each and every light illumine the ten directions with immeasurable bliss and the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi—may I attain rebirth!
May the sufferings and hardships of the three realms and six paths cease, and with immeasurable bliss and manifold marks and signs, may I fulfill the eighty-four thousand vows and attain rebirth;
In the land of Amitābha Buddha, there is no assembly [of suffering]—may I attain immeasurable bliss!
The Joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: I vow to be born there; May the sufferings of the three realms and six paths cease, and immeasurable joy prevail.

Like one suffering from a chronic illness or traveling a long distance without reckoning the days, I vow to be born there; To recollect the Buddha is itself the Way, requiring no effort—immeasurable joy!
The Joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: I vow to be born there; May the sufferings of the three realms and six paths cease, and immeasurable joy prevail.
The three realms offer no peace, like a house on fire; I vow to be reborn there. In the open space at the crossroads, free from all dust, there is immeasurable joy;
in the joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi, I vow to be reborn there. The sufferings of the three realms and six paths never cease;

in immeasurable joy, weary of dwelling in the abode of birth and death, I vow to be reborn among my kin. How could one remain within the five aggregates or dwell in the womb? In immeasurable joy, [I vow to be reborn].

The Joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: May I aspire to be born there; May the sufferings of the three realms and six paths cease—this immeasurable joy is truly attained when one resolves to seek the Way and aspires to be born there in this very life.
Rarely encountered is the opening of the Dharma-gate of the Pure Land—this immeasurable joy. The Joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi:
May I aspire to be born there; May the sufferings of the three realms and six paths cease—this immeasurable joy.
May I attain rebirth in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing in the West; May the holy assembly of Amitābha graciously escort me—may I attain rebirth in immeasurable bliss.
May the sufferings of the three realms and six paths cease; May I attain rebirth in immeasurable bliss through both the gates of meditative concentration and distraction.
May all nine grades, whether refined or coarse, ascend the lotus pedestal—may I attain rebirth in immeasurable bliss.
Through the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi, I vow to be reborn there; May the sufferings of the three realms and six paths cease, and may immeasurable bliss reach that place.
Through the bliss of the three knowledges and eight liberations, I vow to be reborn there; Forever parting from the five turbidities, I shall behold the Tathāgata.
Through the immeasurable bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi, I vow to be reborn there; May the sufferings of the three realms and six paths cease, and may immeasurable bliss prevail.
The vows and practices of Amitābha are vast and boundless; I vow to be reborn there. With compassionate salvation for all beings, he universally cherishes them all;
In the joy of the Immeasurable Life and the joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi, I vow to be reborn there. The sufferings and hardships of the three realms and six paths cannot cease;
He desires to transform all and lead them back to his own land, yet sentient beings’ karmic offenses create no affinity with him.
Text of Mutual Contemplation and Praise The Udumbara flower appears but rarely; Great assembly, listen with focused minds!
Alas, you who sink into the realms of the five desires, Entrusting yourselves to the dark womb of rebirth, The subtle winds blow and fill you with vital breath.
Rarely does this form appear, having emerged from the body—alas! The Udumbara flower appears but rarely; Great assembly, listen with focused minds! Alas!
May she bring joy to her retinue; Che-kang, Nong-ling-hsieh. At first she taught him to hold [a flower] in his palm;
this rarely appearing one, the Compassionate Mother, follows the body in her grace and pity. Utpala flower. Great assembly, listen with focused minds!
This Compassionate One, with her bamboo horse, wanders through forest lanes. In the village, she levels the sand mounds; her two brows are parted like willow leaves—this rarely appearing one.
Her two cheeks are like the luster of peach blossoms—*utpala*. Great assembly, listen with a focused mind!
Chailian, in her years she has passed thirty or five; She devoted herself solely to the pursuit of beauty and splendor.
Carrying her lute, she drinks until the night’s end, hoping to appear before the gaze of others as she gazes upon the morning glow—*utpala*. Great assembly, listen with a focused mind! Chailian.
Abounding in beauty and spirit, leaping with vigor, Arrogant and acting as a hero, He roams upon a dragon-horse;
rarely appearing, he lingers amidst lutes and wine. O Utpala Flower! Great assembly, listen with focused minds:
Cailian sits facing me, gazing at the bright moon; Cailian sits alone, passing through the clear breeze, Holding in hand the sword of Xiangru—rarely appearing.
Fearless of birth and death, like an archer; The *utpala* flower. Great assembly, listen with a focused mind!
Drawing my sword to level the four seas, Holding my halberd to face ten thousand men. One morning upon my pillow, I longed to rise and sit, yet required support from others.
Alas! A deep sigh of lamentation— Who would have known that old age had encroached?

At eighty, my strength is failing and I appear frail; All things are unbearable, and I am weary of this life. O Great Assembly, listen with a focused mind! I have endured the accumulation of frost and dew;

Fearing further invasion by wind and rain, I wish to cultivate the karma for the Western Land. There is nothing better than the vigor of youth; O Utpala Flower, may you appear! Fearing further invasion by wind and rain, I wish to cultivate the karma for the Western Land. There is nothing better than the vigor of youth; O Utpala Flower, may you appear!
Great assembly, listen with focused minds, Cailian! The days one dwells in this world are few;
Lying upon the earth for many years, skulls separate from bones and scatter, rarely appearing again. Flesh is severed and sinews are stripped away, Cailian!
Rarely does the *utpala* flower appear; Great assembly, listen with focused minds, Cailian! Limbs and joints are all overturned, Turning instead into sharp, swirling eddies.

It is as rare as the appearance of an *utpala* flower; O Great Assembly, listen with a focused mind! Even if one diligently pursues the good, in the end, consciousness is but dull and heavy.
