A Praise of the Joy of Renunciation The joy of renunciation! The joy of renunciation!
Having departed from beginningless existence, one is freed from all attachments.
In this life, having encountered the virtuous, one severs ties with kin and worldly relations.
Suddenly casting off coarse emotions,
severing all evils, and exerting body and mind,
one relies on the noble training to eliminate the fetters and afflictions.
The golden razor was lowered to shave his hair;
he donned robes and partook of the jewels of food and medicine.
Consuming these jewels of food and medicine, he conceived the joy of the Dharma, which intensified into exultation.
Who, through the long night, has slept in deep darkness? Today, purify your body!
Rejoice in the Great Awakening! Rejoice in the Great Awakening!
Leave the household life! Be at peace in leaving the household life!
All worldly affairs did not concern him.
Upon reaching the age of twenty,
he met a Venerable Master and respectfully received the śīla.
Meeting a pure altar, meeting a pure altar—
cultivating concentration and wisdom to realize the truth is not difficult.
When awakening is like lapis lazuli, clarity pervades both within and without.
Exquisite as a lotus flower;
behold it freely, behold it fully!
He is called a son of the Śākyas.
The Dharma-gate is broad for entering and exiting;
it is the unimpeded path of coming and going.
Through the path of liberation, one realizes Nirvana from afar.
Consciousness recognizes Nirvana and returns;
the jewel gate opens, and right view beholds Amitābha.
Ascending the jewel throne, the Bodhisattvas scatter flowers.
"Excellent! Excellent! he exclaimed.
As he gazed upon the waterfowl and the groves of jewel-trees, he called to mind the fivefold assembly’s compassionate and plaintive voice.
Praise the Dharma King! Praise the Dharma King!
Like the *jīvamjīvaka* birds, ruddy sheldrakes, parrots, and kalaviṅkas, they proclaim the sublime Dharma and constantly extol all sentient beings.
Dwelling in the realm of suffering, dwelling in the realm of suffering, return!
Depart from Sahā and dwell eternally with the Tathāgata.
"Listen to the wondrous Dharma and receive instruction for the Western Land.
This is Śākyamuni, this is Śākyamuni. Return!"
Behold Amitābha now in the Western Quarter,
manifesting the preaching of the Dharma to ferry sentient beings across;
crossing the river of craving, crossing the river of craving.
Return! Ascend the Golden Terrace;
Śrī-Ārya Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta shall come to lead the way through the *Śata-dharma-viśuddhi-mukha*.
One should open for oneself; one should open for oneself.
Impermanence is swift—do not remain complacent in immeasurable bliss. Like colors upon water, they do not endure long. Amitābha Buddha! Amitābha Buddha!
Conditioned existence exists only briefly and then suddenly vanishes. Immeasurable bliss! Even if a hundred years were but a moment’s blink, Amitābha Buddha! Amitābha Buddha!
All that is born must be impermanent; there is no immeasurable joy. Vigorous beauty does not endure, like a thunderclap that vanishes—Amitābha Buddha!
Amitābha Buddha! Recite the Buddha’s name more and more; do not wander away from immeasurable joy. Today, in this Dharma assembly, we share the same Dharma-joy—Amitābha Buddha! Amitābha Buddha!
From now on, future meetings will likewise be difficult to expect—immeasurable joy! Each person sighs with a joyful countenance and makes a vow together—Amitābha Buddha! Amitābha Buddha!
In the past, there was a Bodhisattva who sat with a settled mind before Amitābha Buddha; He perceived that the five aggregates are entirely empty—Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha.
Within emptiness and signlessness lies a priceless treasure—Amitābha Buddha; The ocean of the nature of Prajñā is inconceivable—Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha.
Thus we know the wondrous body is free from all obstruction—Amitābha Buddha; This is a great divine mantra that gives rise to compassion in people—Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha.
Truly and without falsehood, one must deeply believe in Amitābha Buddha; Gati Gati, severing all doubt, Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was dwelling at the Joyful Bodhimanda on Vulture Peak in Rājagṛha.
The Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and the eight classes of beings were also at the Joyful Bodhimanda. The earth shook and celestial flowers fell—not like any other—within the Joyful Bodhimanda.
This is the joy of the Bodhimaṇḍa where all Buddhas manifest their birth; Mañjuśrī explains the causal conditions of former lives—this is the joy of the Bodhimaṇḍa.
Rays of light shine everywhere, causing all to marvel—this is the joy of the Bodhimaṇḍa;

The great assembly together cultivates the practice for the Pure Land—this is the joy of the Bodhimaṇḍa. Holding incense and flowers in hand, they proceed toward the West—this is the joy of the Bodhimaṇḍa.
When this disciple makes their vow, may there be great bliss;

May they dwell upon Mount Wutai, where the Great Blissful Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva hears the heart-ground of the sons of Bodhisattvas; Upon the lotus pedestal of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, may there be great bliss;
When this disciple makes their vow, may there be great bliss; May they realize the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, may there be great bliss.
The Great Bliss of the Chapter on the Place of Faith in the Avataṃsaka Sūtra; the Great Bliss of the Bodhisattva Citta-rāja dwelling therein;
the Great Bliss when the disciples of Great Bliss make their vows; the Great Bliss of the aspiration to become a son of the Buddha’s disciples within the ocean of the Buddha-nature of Nirvāṇa;
the Great Bliss of the early realization of the great mountain of Nirvāṇa—Great Bliss! Great Bliss!

When the disciple makes this vow, there is great bliss; May I become a son of the Bodhisattva of the Great Bliss of the Twelve Vows of Bhaiṣajyaguru, as expressed in the *Bhaiṣajyaguru Sūtra*. May every vow deliver all sentient beings—great bliss, great bliss!
When the disciple makes this vow, there is great bliss; May I become [a son of] the Great Bliss of the *Avalokiteśvara Sūtra*.
The power of Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta is Great Bliss; When first entering the place of suffering, one attains Great Bliss;
when the disciples of Great Bliss make their vows, it is Great Bliss.

May they become the sons of Bodhisattvas within the sixteen contemplations of the *Sūtra of Immeasurable Life*, the Sūtra of Great Bliss; Through samādhi, they naturally achieve Great Bliss—Great Bliss!

When the disciple makes this vow, there is great bliss; May I become a lamp before the Buddha, with great bliss illuminating the sutras and the Bodhisattva images—great bliss. May I illuminate my teachers and monks, great bliss;
when the disciple makes this vow, there is great bliss. May I become an incense lamp for the Buddha, a son of the Bodhisattvas—great bliss.
Offering lamps and incense to the Buddha is great bliss; Delivering those with karmic affinity from cyclic existence is great bliss;
When disciples make their aspirational prayers, it is great bliss; May there be a pool of the seven precious jewels—great bliss;
Within that pool are noble Bodhisattvas—great bliss; All who are reborn there are great bliss—great bliss.
Sublime is Amitābha, his countenance of purple-gold form;
His physical marks are the thirty-two, And his secondary characteristics are the eighty; His radiance constantly shines with brilliance.
The Brahma-voice transcends the three thousandfold world; its wondrous resonance is like the mournful cry of the phoenix.
Sublime is Amitābha, whose land is exceedingly pure and bright, entirely of golden hue, where even the name of the four evil women does not exist.

The waters of the ponds flow and pour into one another; The jeweled trees produce the five musical tones, singing and praising impermanence and suffering. Those who hear this attain the state of non-arising;
Amitābha is most sublime, the sovereign of all virtues.
The land is wondrously peaceful and blissful; there is no one who does not aspire to be reborn there.
The Buddhas and the assembly of Bodhisattvas fly forth together to welcome them.
Suddenly, within a pond of the seven treasures, they grow to maturity amidst lotus flowers.
Sublime is Amitābha, whose majestic virtue is wondrous and peerless;
His body is of true golden color, radiating light throughout the lands of the ten directions.
Whoever hears of him, beholds him, or encounters him, Shall forever uproot the suffering of birth and death.
I now prostrate in homage to the supreme among sentient beings.

When sentient beings are beset by distress, And their bodies are oppressed by immeasurable suffering, The wondrous power of Avalokiteśvara’s wisdom Is able to rescue the world from its pain. And so forth...
When caught in legal disputes before government officials, or amidst the terrors of battle arrays,
by recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, all enemies shall retreat and disperse.
With wondrous voice, voice that observes the world, Brahma-voice, and ocean-tide voice—
His voice surpasses that of the world; therefore, one should constantly recite his name at every thought and never give rise to doubt.
Avalokiteśvara, the pure and holy one, can act as a refuge for those in suffering, distress, and the perils of death.
Possessing all merits, Beholding sentient beings with eyes of compassion, An ocean of immeasurable accumulations of merit— Therefore, one should pay homage with the crown of the head.
Praise to the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta! Praise to the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta! Praise to the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta!
With great mastery of supernormal powers,
they are equal to Avalokiteśvara without distinction.
These two Great Beings, Avalokiteśvara and Śākyamuni (Śrī-ghoṣa), [are present].
They constantly attend upon Amitābha Buddha at his left and right.
Avalokiteśvara wears Amitābha Buddha upon his crown,
while Śrīkṣetra has a precious flask within his crown.
The light within the vase is immeasurably vast;
it constantly radiates brilliance to illuminate sentient beings in suffering.
Through loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity, it perpetually gathers and sustains all beings.
Whatever deeds are performed are never in vain;
therefore, I pay homage from afar to the Great Sage Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva— praise to the Great Sage Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Mañjuśrī!
The son of the Dharma King Wondrous Virtue,
he is the patriarchal teacher of the seven Buddhas,
titled the Buddha Dragon-Species Supreme Honored King.
Although they attain the Buddha-way, turn the wheel of Dharma, and enter nirvana,
they do not abandon the path of the bodhisattva,
continuing to teach and transform sentient beings.
Immeasurable merits are all fully accomplished;
immeasurable Buddha-lands are all adorned and purified.
Those who see or hear [this] shall all receive benefit.
Whatever he does is never in vain. At present,
he dwells within Mount Qingliang in the world of Suvarṇa in the northeastern direction,
abiding in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
Together with ten thousand bodhisattvas,
you assemble to bring benefit and happiness to suffering sentient beings;
therefore, I pay homage to you from afar.
First, visualize the sun in the west: Amitābha Buddha, Sit upright with body straight and dispel all confusion:
Amitābha Buddha. Namo Amitābha Buddha. When you see him about to set like a suspended drum: Amitābha Buddha, To make the mind firm, do not let it rise or fall:

Amitābha Buddha. Namo Amitābha Buddha. Second, visualize that water is originally clear: Amitābha Buddha, Contemplate the water as ice; this principle is easily accomplished: Amitābha Buddha. Namo Amitābha Buddha.
Causing the ice to reflect as a floor of lapis lazuli, Amitābha Buddha— Clearly one sees again the jeweled banners being upheld, Amitābha Buddha. *Namo Amitābha Buddha*.
Third, within the precious ground, golden Amitābha Buddha— At the six periods of the day, rains of flowers fill the jade grove, Amitābha Buddha. *Namo Amitābha Buddha*.
Dividing its radiance, it transforms into music in the sky, Amitābha Buddha— The flutes and pipes can purify the minds of practitioners, Amitābha Buddha. *Namo Amitābha Buddha*.
The Fourth: The Treasure Trees of Seven Jewels in Rows, Amitābha Buddha; The Leaves Spread and Branches Dangle with Wondrously Colored Light, Amitābha Buddha. *Namo Amitābha Buddha*.
The Flowers and Leaves Are Fully Present Throughout the Four Seasons, Amitābha Buddha; When the Wind Comes Under the Forest, It Further Spreads Fragrance, Amitābha Buddha.

*Namo Amitābha Buddha*. The Fifth: One Should Contemplate the Pools of Seven Jewels, Amitābha Buddha; Pure, Cool, and Endowed with the Eight Virtues, Inconceivable, Amitābha Buddha. *Namo Amitābha Buddha*.
The canals are all waters of golden sand; Amitābha Buddha. Upon the waters, flowers bloom without end; Amitābha Buddha. Namo Amitābha Buddha. (Sixth:
One should contemplate the Tower of Many Jewels. Amitābha Buddha. Pearl-pavilions and jade-steps in the autumn of azure clouds; Amitābha Buddha. Namo Amitābha Buddha.

When celestial music plays, its sound resonates through the clear night; Amitābha Buddha. The Dharma-sound is subtle and wondrous, exhorting us to diligent cultivation; Amitābha Buddha. Namo Amitābha Buddha.
Seventh: Solely contemplate the flower seat opening to reveal Amitābha Buddha— With leaves of gold and a pedestal of jade, Amitābha Buddha. Namo Amitābha Buddha.
A jeweled banner covered with a net of pearls, Amitābha Buddha— Its adornment intended solely for the Tathāgata, Amitābha Buddha. Namo Amitābha Buddha. Eighth:
The precious image, its color perfect and luminous, Amitābha Buddha— All phenomena arise from the mind’s conception, Amitābha Buddha. Namo Amitābha Buddha.
If one sees his body seated upon a flower, Amitābha Buddha; The profound samādhi spontaneously accomplishes Amitābha Buddha.

Sentient beings who practice mindfulness of the Buddha are all gathered in, Amitābha Buddha; His mind never abandons those with whom he has a karmic connection, Amitābha Buddha. *Namo Amitābha Buddha*.
Tenth: The Honored One Who Succeeds Avalokiteśvara, Amitābha Buddha. Your body shares the marks of a Buddha, wondrous beyond discourse.

Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha. You uphold the Tathāgata in your heart with deep reverence. Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha. Eleventh: The Great Majestic Hero, Śrī-akṣobhya (Potisai) Buddha.
As a successor, you have long vibrated throughout the six realms. Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.

The World-Treasury of Infinite Light, who shakes the world to deliver those ready for salvation; Amitābha Buddha. His radiance constantly shines upon those who practice; Amitābha Buddha. *Namo Amitābha Buddha*.
Twelve times contemplating the body, one is born spontaneously in the Pure Land; Amitābha Buddha. The lotus flowers open and close with extreme clarity;

Amitābha Buddha. *Namo Amitābha Buddha*. Sitting upright and serene, the mind unmoving; Amitābha Buddha. At the moment of death, one shall behold the Buddha coming to welcome them; Amitābha Buddha. *Namo Amitābha Buddha*.
Amitābha Buddha, with a body of thirteen *zhang* and six *chi* of purple-golden hue— The true and the manifested have always been non-dual; Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.
Provided one contemplates according to the mind until it is clear and distinct— The wondrous marks of the Dharma-body appear naturally, grain by grain; Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.
The life and deeds of those born in the fourteenth grade are sublime— Those of the superior grade possess the noble lineage of the three minds; Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.
Amitābha Buddha of the Gate of Illumination of the Hundred Dharmas, the Ground of Joy; Amitābha Buddha whose Vajra-Samadhi Power is Transformed and Firm; Homage to Amitābha Buddha.
Amitābha Buddha who dwells among the nine grades for fifteen lifetimes; Amitābha Buddha whose pure precepts refine past karma until it is harmonized; Homage to Amitābha Buddha.

Amitābha Buddha who, through the instructions of virtuous friends, turns one’s vows toward rebirth [in his land]; Amitābha Buddha in whom one is suddenly awakened while sitting within a lotus palace; Homage to Amitābha Buddha.
Amitābha Buddha, whose station as a later rebirth is most lowly; Amitābha Buddha, whose karmic obstructions are difficult to dissolve and whose wisdom awakens slowly. Homage to Amitābha Buddha!
Though one dwells for kalpas within the lotus womb, Amitābha Buddha, upon the blossoming of the flower, one still attains the realization of non-arising. Homage to Amitābha Buddha!
Śākyamuni, the Great Compassionate World-Honored One, Amitābha Buddha, Who first opened the gate of the Pure Land to save the world. Homage to Amitābha Buddha! Homage to Amitābha Buddha!
I wish to speak of the adornment of the Land of Ultimate Bliss and Amitābha Buddha. At that time, he was in the Jeta Grove; Homage to Amitābha Buddha! Homage to Amitābha Buddha!

The Wheel of Dharma is about to arise, with many disciples listening; Amitābha Buddha! Immeasurable hosts of devas and the great assembly are all present; Homage to Amitābha Buddha! Homage to Amitābha Buddha!
The foremost Śrāvaka is Śāriputra; Amitābha Buddha! The Bodhisattva of the Supreme Vehicle is Mañjuśrī; Homage to Amitābha Buddha! Homage to Amitābha Buddha!
At the time when the True Dharma was first proclaimed, Amitābha Buddha— To the west, beyond ten koṭis of worlds from here, is the world-realm named Sukhāvatī, adorned with splendor;
Amitābha Buddha! Amitābha dwells there in the inconceivable; Namu Amitābha Buddha! Namu Amitābha Buddha!
The suffering of the sentient beings in that land has already been removed; Amitābha Buddha! There is nothing but pure, tranquil, and supreme bliss; Namu Amitābha Buddha! Namu Amitābha Buddha!
Practicing day and night, one transcends the eight difficulties; Amitābha Buddha—His form and features are dignified and majestic, all as one.
Namo Amitābha Buddha. Namo Amitābha Buddha. Seven layers of walking trees, seven layers of railings; Amitābha Buddha—Jeweled canopies hang in the void, with jeweled nets and bells.

Namo Amitābha Buddha. Namo Amitābha Buddha. All who possess the karmic affinity shall behold Amitābha Buddha; those who study with earnestness should contemplate Him with their whole hearts. Namo Amitābha Buddha. Namo Amitābha Buddha.
People arrive to ride upon flowers and sit within the jeweled groves; Amitābha Buddha. Devas come to play music with melodies profound and subtle;

Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha. The Six Perfections have already harmonized the six musical notes; Amitābha Buddha. The Eightfold Path further blends the eight tones; Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.
In the precious pond of virtuous water, the sand at the bottom is fresh; Amitābha Buddha. The lotus blooms with a radiance like the wheels of a chariot; Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.
The Bodhisattvas sit upright upon lotus flowers; Amitābha Buddha— When one looks, they are all people who have been reborn there.
*Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.* In the Dharma-king’s Pure Land of Maitreya, Amitābha Buddha— The power of his vows adorns and brings forth the sprouts of the Way.

*Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.* Within the jade-green pavilion, precious thrones fly about; Amitābha Buddha— Upon the golden ground, heavenly flowers rain down. *Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.*

Having gathered heavenly flowers in his robe-sleeve, he offers them to Amitābha Buddha; In the six realms, his body is light through the realization of *yathābhūta*. Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.
Having made offerings to the Buddhas of other lands, Amitābha Buddha Returns to his own land to eat and walk in meditation.

Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha. The flocks of birds harmonize their voices throughout the six periods; Amitābha Buddha’s pure sounds expound the Dharma, wondrous and inconceivable. Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.

The five powers and the five faculties, together with the seven factors of enlightenment—Amitābha Buddha! The profound eightfold noble path enters the unconditioned—Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha!
The assembly together listens to the sound of the Dharma—Amitābha Buddha! All who hear it give rise to the mind of mindfulness of the Buddha—Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha!
The transformed birds were originally not of the three evil realms—Amitābha Buddha! Amitābha proclaims the deep flow of the Dharma—Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha!
A gentle breeze stirs the jewel groves, and the pure sound of Amitābha Buddha’s name resounds like celestial music.
Homage to Amitābha Buddha! Homage to Amitābha Buddha! In every place, no other teaching is proclaimed; everywhere one hears only the name of the Buddha of Recollection.
Homage to Amitābha Buddha! Homage to Amitābha Buddha! The lifespan of Amitābha is truly boundless; so too is it for the people within his land. Homage to Amitābha Buddha! Homage to Amitābha Buddha!
It has been ten kalpas since Amitābha Buddha attained the Way; His light illuminates the dharma-realms and lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Homage to Amitābha Buddha! Homage to Amitābha Buddha! The assembly of Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas is exceedingly vast; Amitābha Buddha appears for those seeking liberation.

Homage to Amitābha Buddha! Homage to Amitābha Buddha! Its measure cannot be known through calculation; Buddhas from all other directions also come to visit. Homage to Amitābha Buddha! Homage to Amitābha Buddha!
It is heard that the Pure Land is exceedingly pure and true; Amitābha Buddha, Its inhabitants are all those who have attained the stage of non-retrogression (*avaivartika*).

*Namo Amitābha Buddha*, *Namo Amitābha Buddha*. Those in their final birth before Buddhahood cultivate samādhi; Amitābha Buddha, They have realized the adamantine final body. *Namo Amitābha Buddha*, *Namo Amitābha Buddha*.

Those with meager roots of goodness and little merit find it difficult to be born there by principle; Amitābha Buddha, For seven days they must single-mindedly recite the Buddha’s name. *Namo Amitābha Buddha*, *Namo Amitābha Buddha*.
If, at the moment of death, one’s mind is undisturbed, Amitābha Buddha will surely come to welcome them in person.

*Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.* Amitābha, with his ten titles, repays past causes. *Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.* The Buddhas of the six directions bear witness to His truth.

*Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.* His tongue is broad and long, free from falsehood. *Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.* The Tathāgata protects those who possess faith. *Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.*
The world is impermanent and difficult to remain in for long; Amitābha Buddha— One must simply make vows and seek with diligent effort. Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.

Those already born and those yet to be born all attain non-retrogression; Amitābha Buddha— How could this be limited to whether one has practiced now or not? Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.
All Buddhas simultaneously praise Śākyamuni and Amitābha Buddha— Able to rescue the Sahā world amidst the five turbidities. Namo Amitābha Buddha, Namo Amitābha Buddha.
He has preached this Dharma difficult for this world to believe—Amitābha Buddha; May all be awakened and led to enlightenment—Homage to Amitābha Buddha, Homage to Amitābha Buddha.
The treasury of the Dharma has been fully expounded in its meaning—Amitābha Buddha; From this, Ānanda shall propagate the true exposition—Homage to Amitābha Buddha, Homage to Amitābha Buddha.

The great assembly rejoices and all receive it upon their heads—Amitābha Buddha; The Tathāgata’s entrustment is complete; let it be widely disseminated—Homage to Amitābha Buddha, Homage to Amitābha Buddha.
Śākyamuni dwells on Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa; Amitābha Buddha has appeared in this world to transform the Sahā world. *Namo Amitābha Buddha*.
With an immeasurable assembly of Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and others, Amitābha Buddha—though he first desired to hear the sutra, his mind was not yet at ease.

The Wise One’s compassion transmits the five assemblies, With the intent to transmit them so as to extinguish the five burnings.
Since the five burnings are extinguished by means of the five assemblies, All rely upon the five assemblies to transcend worldly toil.
Majestic and resonant, the fivefold assembly utters pure sounds; Deep and rumbling, the thunderous voice articulates wondrous tones.
The holy multitudes join together in praise; Whoever hears it shall all resolve their minds [for enlightenment].
These subtle and exquisite five-toned voices from the Western Land Shall come to rescue sentient beings in the future age of the five turbidities.
The five destinies, upon hearing his name, are all liberated; The five assemblies lead the way to the City of Precious Lotuses.
The fifth assembly emerges from Mount Heng; Its resonance now pervades the Five Regions.
The five groups of disciples all speak of benefit and joy; In the Dharma-ending age, he remains for another five hundred years.
The five assemblies of Amitābha penetrate the human heart; His mournful and compassionate voice is profound and winding.
As the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* describes it, The precious waters remain forever, chanting wondrous sounds.
The resonance of the five assemblies rises through the clouds and mists; Its pure tones, vast and resonant, pervade as many worlds as grains of sand.
May one be able to maintain mindfulness morning and night, And be born within the Buddha’s family in every life and every rebirth.
When fragrant breezes arise and touch the body, They shall sever greed and anger through the five assemblies of mantras;
The five tones can simultaneously purify the five aggregates, And by hearing the name, one shall leave behind the clamor and dust for five kalpas.
In the western quarter, drums and music, along with stringed songs—zithers, lutes, flutes, and pipes—all blend together in harmony;
each and every note proclaims the Dharma of the Five Assemblies, and every sound expounds the six *pāramitās*.
Amitābha’s vows and practices are vast and boundless; with compassion, he rescues all sentient beings, pitying them universally and exhaustively.
Wishing in general to transform and lead them back to their own land, Sentient beings, through their karmic offenses,
lack the conditions [to see him]. Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, with great compassion,
Is able to manifest within the sea of suffering a rare body of purple-golden hue with the thirty-two marks, Upon whose crown he reverently bears Amitābha.
The Bodhisattva Śrīkṣetra is most difficult to conceive; His body of purple-gold, its marks and signs complete without flaw.
A precious vase atop his head radiates brilliant light, Universally gathering those with the karmic affinity for mindfulness of the Buddha and rebirth in the Pure Land.
I rejoice that my past roots of merit were deep, That I have encountered the sound of Amitābha’s pure teachings.
Holding fast to the Name without ceasing, when my life-span ends at the moment of death, may I possess a body of purple-gold.
I have always lamented my own lack of diligent effort; I long to hear the unsurpassed, pure, and true Dharma.
We must join together to battle the thief of ignorance; I vow to utterly destroy it and seize the true gold.
In a single thought, concentrate the spirit and go to the Precious City; Rouse the six supernormal powers and awaken to the lightness of the body.
With feet treading upon thousand-petaled lotuses, Walk beneath the moon-bright maṇi trees.
The Pure Land of Amitābha is most subtle and profound; How could the people of this Sahā world ever know it?
Sunk for vast eons in the ocean of suffering, when will the year come that we encounter the time of rebirth?
In the precious land of Ultimate Bliss there is no decay; its jade-green towers and terraces are spontaneously formed by heaven.
With mani-jewels, bright moons, and lapis lazuli waters, the radiant ponds and pavilions are truly lovely.
The precious realm of Ultimate Bliss is most rare; Truly, throughout many lifetimes, it has remained unknown.
Today, meeting the Honored One Amitābha with joy, I suddenly abandon the five turbidities of Saṃsāra.
The precious realm of Amitābha is inconceivable; I can only sigh that those who depart from Saṃsāra are few.
Many people go to the Avīci Hell; once fallen there, how many years will it take before they emerge?
Come back! Come back! This Jambudvīpa of the five turbidities is but dust and grime;
it is not like the joyful land in the West, where one arrives to find the lotus pedestal opening at will.

The causes of Dharmakara are most remote; The fruit of Sukhāvatī is likewise profound. Rare treasures combine to form its ground.
Forests interspersed with various jewels, Flowers blooming in rare and wondrous colors, Waves surging with the sound of the true nature— When shall I receive your reaching hand?

A bystander said, "This is your child. Hearing this, the mother called out in joy, forgetting the pain that bound her body.
Though she herself was in a damp place, she took her child back to the dry ground;

with blood and milk she satisfied his hunger and thirst, shielding him from wind and cold with her coarse robes. She gave him sweet things without stinginess, and swallowed bitterness without a frown.
Providing only that her child be sated, the compassionate mother does not refuse hunger; as the years pass and the child gradually grows, she follows his heart wherever he goes.
One morning, when the son and daughter fall ill, she regrets that it was not her own body that was stricken.
The pain of loving separation is difficult to endure; the sorrow of parting truly knots the bowels. Even if the child travels but a hundred li within, [the mother’s grief remains].
The compassionate mother has over a thousand sons; When the men grow up, they are drafted for military service, And when the women reach maturity, they serve in others' households.
When the winter season and the year-end festivals arrive, The compassionate mother’s sighs moisten her breast.
Every day she longs for her children, questioning them frequently whenever she meets them. If she receives good news, She prepares fine food and cultivates fields of merit.
Though parents have grown old, their compassionate affection never ceases; even at a hundred years of age, they long for their children of eighty.
Thus one knows that the weight of love and affection is such that even now, when the five consciousnesses have separated and one has departed for the Yellow Springs, one does not abandon them;
even as a ghost, one still grieves for them. This is true for all who are sons and daughters.

Riding upon a lotus, they entrust themselves to the womb within the mani-water; Enveloped by flowers, only upon opening do they hear the sound of liberation.
